23 Chapter 4: detailed summary

Introduction — messages are events you can program

  • An event-driven system reacts to signals: mouse movement raises X/Y coordinate events, a key press raises a key event. The OS raises thousands of events per millisecond, mostly invisible to the user.
  • At OS level one form of event is a message: a click calls the window procedure for the window under the cursor, passing a message code and event-specific details such as coordinates.
  • A top-level window must implement a handler (WindowProcedure/WndProc). The main thread's window queue can receive messages from other threads; PostThreadMessage is the alternative when there is no UI, but the target thread must own a message queue.

Recipe 1 — Basic Message Passing Interface

  • basic_MPI.cpp registers a window class, creates a main window plus three child controls (two BUTTONs and one STATIC label), and runs the standard GetMessage → TranslateMessage → DispatchMessage loop.
  • Child-control IDs (BUTTON_MSG, BUTTON_CLOSE, LABEL_TEXT) are passed in the hMenu argument of CreateWindow. They must be unique per parent window and are how a child notifies its parent.
  • In WM_COMMAND, the low word of wParam identifies the control: "Show msg" opens a topmost message box; "Close me" posts WM_CLOSE.
  • WM_MOUSEMOVE uses GET_X_LPARAM/GET_Y_LPARAM to extract coordinates and writes them into the label with SetWindowText. WM_DESTROY calls PostQuitMessage; unhandled messages go to DefWindowProc.
  • Messages are easier than specialised synchronisation objects when a worker simply needs to say "I'm done" to the UI thread.

Recipe 2 — A message queue for producer/consumer work

  • Scenario: draw a four-axis plot while several calculation threads produce results faster than the single drawing thread can render them. The solution is a queue between producers and consumer.
  • queue_MPI.cpp defines user messages above WM_USER (1024): WM_PLOTDATA for "result ready" and WM_ENDTASK for "drawing complete". Custom messages leave wParam/lParam to the application — here lParam carries a PLOTDATA*.
  • Four calculation threads enqueue PLOTDATA into a CQueue<PLOTDATA> under a CRITICAL_SECTION, then PostMessage(hWnd, WM_PLOTDATA, 0, (LPARAM)pData). One draw thread waits on a named event, dequeues under the same critical section, sleeps to simulate slower drawing, updates the label and deletes the object.
  • The queue's address can be attached to the window with SetWindowLongPtr(hWnd, GWLP_USERDATA, ...) and recovered with GetWindowLongPtr. Calculation sleep is 1 s versus 2.3 s for drawing, deliberately creating a backlog.
  • PostMessage vs SendMessage: posting returns immediately; sending waits for the callee to process the message. Messages are fetched with GetMessage or PeekMessage.

Recipe 3 — Thread message queues without a window

  • threadMPI.cpp defines T_MESSAGE ("do the task") and T_ENDTASK ("application is closing"). A worker thread that owns no window has no message queue, so it calls PeekMessage(&msg, NULL, WM_USER, WM_USER, PM_NOREMOVE) to force the OS to create one.
  • The main thread creates an event, starts the worker, saves its thread ID in window user data, and waits for the worker to signal that the queue exists before posting anything.
  • A button in WM_COMMAND retrieves the ID with GetWindowLongPtr and calls PostThreadMessage(id, T_MESSAGE, 0, 0). The worker's own GetMessage loop switches on the message: show a message box, or return on T_ENDTASK.
  • On shutdown the main thread posts T_ENDTASK, waits on the thread handle and closes it. The book's analogy is a weather application: one thread reads physical sensors, another waits for and displays the collected data.

Recipe 4 — Named pipes for process communication

  • A pipe is an in-memory object with two ends: the creator is the server, the connector is the client. One writes, the other reads. The example name is \\.\pipe\basicMPI.
  • pipe_server.cpp loops forever: CreateNamedPipe with PIPE_ACCESS_DUPLEX, blocking message mode and unlimited instances; ConnectNamedPipe blocks until a client arrives; each connection is handed to a new thread so the main loop can accept the next client.
  • The worker thread allocates request/reply buffers on the process heap, reads the request with ReadFile, writes a "default answer from server" with WriteFile, then FlushFileBuffers, DisconnectNamedPipe, CloseHandle and frees the buffers.
  • pipe_client.cpp opens the pipe with CreateFile, waits with WaitNamedPipe, sets PIPE_READMODE_MESSAGE via SetNamedPipeHandleState, writes a message and reads the reply in a loop (handling ERROR_MORE_DATA), then closes the handle. CallNamedPipe is a simpler alternative.
  • The chapter closes by encouraging combination of the techniques: message queues, thread queues and pipes each solve a different communication shape.

57queue_MPI.cpp — four producers, one drawer, CQueue<PLOTDATA>book pp. 148–154 · PDF pp. 163–169▼

#include <windows.h>
#include <windowsx.h>
#include <tchar.h>
#include "CQueue.h"
#include <commctrl.h>

#pragma comment ( lib, "comctl32.lib" )
#pragma comment ( linker, "\"/manifestdependency:type='win32' \
name='Microsoft.Windows.Common-Controls' \
version='6.0.0.0' processorArchitecture='*' \
publicKeyToken='6595b64144ccf1df' language='*'\"" )

#define BUFFER_SIZE    4096

#define LABEL_TEXT    100

#define WM_PLOTDATA  WM_USER    + 1
#define WM_ENDTASK  WM_PLOTDATA + 1

#define THREAD_NUMBER  4
#define MAX_MSGCOUNT  10

#define CALCULATION_TIME  1000

#define DRAWING_TIME    2300

#define EVENT_NAME    _T( "__t_event__" )

typedef struct tagPLOTDATA
{
  int value;
  DWORD dwThreadId;
  int iMsgID;
} PLOTDATA, *PPLOTDATA;

LRESULT CALLBACK WindowProcedure(HWND hWnd, UINT uMsg, WPARAM
wParam, LPARAM lParam);
DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter);
DWORD WINAPI DrawPlot(LPVOID lpParameter);

int iMessageID = 0;
HANDLE gEvent = NULL;
HANDLE hThreads[THREAD_NUMBER];
HANDLE hThread = NULL;

CRITICAL_SECTION cs;
CQueue<PLOTDATA> queue;

int WINAPI _tWinMain(HINSTANCE hThis, HINSTANCE hPrev, LPTSTR
szCommandLine, int iWndShow)
{
  UNREFERENCED_PARAMETER(hPrev);
  UNREFERENCED_PARAMETER(szCommandLine);

  InitializeCriticalSection(&cs);

  TCHAR* szWindowClass = _T("__basic_MPI_wnd_class__");

  WNDCLASSEX wndEx = { 0 };
  wndEx.cbSize = sizeof(WNDCLASSEX);
  wndEx.style = CS_HREDRAW | CS_VREDRAW;
  wndEx.lpfnWndProc = WindowProcedure;
  wndEx.cbClsExtra = 0;
  wndEx.cbWndExtra = 0;
  wndEx.hInstance = hThis;
  wndEx.hIcon = LoadIcon(wndEx.hInstance,
    MAKEINTRESOURCE(IDI_APPLICATION));
  wndEx.hCursor = LoadCursor(NULL, IDC_ARROW);

  wndEx.hbrBackground = (HBRUSH)(COLOR_WINDOW + 1);
  wndEx.lpszMenuName = NULL;
  wndEx.lpszClassName = szWindowClass;
  wndEx.hIconSm = LoadIcon(wndEx.hInstance,
    MAKEINTRESOURCE(IDI_APPLICATION));

  if (!RegisterClassEx(&wndEx))
  {
    return 1;
  }

  InitCommonControls();

  HWND hWnd = CreateWindow(szWindowClass, _T("Basic Message
Passing Interface"), WS_OVERLAPPED | WS_CAPTION | WS_SYSMENU |
WS_MINIMIZEBOX, 200, 200, 440, 300, NULL, NULL, wndEx.hInstance,
NULL);

  if (!hWnd)
  {
    return NULL;
  }

  HFONT hFont = CreateFont(14, 0, 0, 0, FW_NORMAL, FALSE,
    FALSE, FALSE, BALTIC_CHARSET, OUT_DEFAULT_PRECIS,
    CLIP_DEFAULT_PRECIS, DEFAULT_QUALITY, DEFAULT_PITCH |
    FF_MODERN, _T("Microsoft Sans Serif"));

  HWND hText = CreateWindow(_T("STATIC"), NULL, WS_CHILD |
    WS_VISIBLE | SS_LEFT | WS_BORDER, 15, 20, 390, 220, hWnd,
    (HMENU)LABEL_TEXT, wndEx.hInstance, NULL);

  SendMessage(hText, WM_SETFONT, (WPARAM)hFont, TRUE);

  ShowWindow(hWnd, iWndShow);

  MSG msg;
  while (GetMessage(&msg, 0, 0, 0))
  {
    TranslateMessage(&msg);
    DispatchMessage(&msg);

  }

  UnregisterClass(wndEx.lpszClassName, wndEx.hInstance);

  WaitForMultipleObjects(THREAD_NUMBER, hThreads, TRUE, INFINITE);

  for (int iIndex = 0; iIndex < THREAD_NUMBER; iIndex++)
  {
    CloseHandle(hThreads[iIndex]);
  }

  WaitForSingleObject(hThread, INFINITE);

  CloseHandle(hThread);
  CloseHandle(gEvent);

  DeleteCriticalSection(&cs);

  return (int)msg.wParam;
}

LRESULT CALLBACK WindowProcedure(HWND hWnd, UINT uMsg, WPARAM
wParam, LPARAM lParam)
{
  switch (uMsg)
  {
    case WM_CREATE:
    {
      gEvent = CreateEvent(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, EVENT_NAME);

      for (int iIndex = 0; iIndex < THREAD_NUMBER; iIndex++)
      {
        hThreads[iIndex] = CreateThread(NULL, 0,
         (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)StartAddress, hWnd, 0, NULL);
      }

      hThread = CreateThread(NULL, 0, (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)
DrawPlot, hWnd, 0, NULL);
      break;
    }
    case WM_PLOTDATA:

    {
      PPLOTDATA pData = (PPLOTDATA)lParam;

      HWND hLabel = GetDlgItem(hWnd, LABEL_TEXT);

      TCHAR szBuffer[BUFFER_SIZE];
      GetWindowText(hLabel, szBuffer, BUFFER_SIZE);

      wsprintf(szBuffer,
        _T("%ws\n\n\tMessage has been received. Msg ID:\t%d"),
        szBuffer, pData->iMsgID);
      SetWindowText(hLabel, szBuffer);

      break;
    }
    case WM_ENDTASK:
    {
      HWND hLabel = GetDlgItem(hWnd, LABEL_TEXT);

      TCHAR szBuffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

      wsprintf(szBuffer,
        _T("\n\n\tPlot is drawn. You can close the window now."));
      SetWindowText(hLabel, szBuffer);
      break;
    }
    case WM_DESTROY:
    {
      PostQuitMessage(0);
      break;
    }
    default:
    {
      return DefWindowProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
    }
  }

  return 0;
}

DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  HWND hWnd = (HWND)lpParameter;

  HANDLE hEvent = OpenEvent(EVENT_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, EVENT_NAME);

  if (hEvent != NULL)
  {
    SetEvent(hEvent);
  }

  CloseHandle(hEvent);

  int iCount = 0;
  while (iCount++ < MAX_MSGCOUNT)
  {
    // perform calculation
    Sleep(CALCULATION_TIME);

    // assembly result into PLOTDATA structure
    PPLOTDATA pData = new PLOTDATA();
    pData->value = (rand() % 0xFFFF) - iMessageID;
    pData->dwThreadId = GetCurrentThreadId();
    pData->iMsgID = ++iMessageID;

    EnterCriticalSection(&cs);
    queue.Enqueue(pData);
    LeaveCriticalSection(&cs);

    PostMessage(hWnd, WM_PLOTDATA, 0, (LPARAM)pData);
  }

  return 0L;
}

DWORD WINAPI DrawPlot(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  HWND hWnd = (HWND)lpParameter;

  HANDLE hEvent = OpenEvent(EVENT_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, EVENT_NAME);

  WaitForSingleObject(hEvent, INFINITE);
  CloseHandle(hEvent);

  int iCount = 0;
  while (iCount++ < MAX_MSGCOUNT * THREAD_NUMBER)
  {
    EnterCriticalSection(&cs);

    PPLOTDATA pData = queue.Dequeue();
    LeaveCriticalSection(&cs);

    if (!pData)
    {
      break;
    }

    // perform drawing
    Sleep(DRAWING_TIME);

    HWND hLabel = GetDlgItem(hWnd, LABEL_TEXT);

    TCHAR szBuffer[BUFFER_SIZE];

  wsprintf(szBuffer,
#ifdef _UNICODE
    _T("\n\n\t%ws\t%u\n\t%ws\t%d\n\t%ws\t%d"),
#else
    _T("\n\n\t%s\t%u\n\t%s\t%d\n\t%s\t%d"),
#endif
    _T("Thread ID:"), (DWORD)pData->dwThreadId,
    _T("Current value:"), (int)pData->value,
    _T("Message ID:"), pData->iMsgID);
    SetWindowText(hLabel, szBuffer);

    delete pData;
  }

  PostMessage(hWnd, WM_ENDTASK, 0, 0);

  return 0L;
}

wParam, LPARAM lParam)
{
  switch (uMsg)
  {
    case WM_COMMAND:
    {
      switch (LOWORD(wParam))
      {
        case BUTTON_CLOSE:
        {
          DWORD* pdwThreadId = (DWORD*)GetWindowLongPtr(hWnd,
GWLP_USERDATA);
          PostThreadMessage(*pdwThreadId, T_MESSAGE, 0, 0);
          break;
        }
      }
      break;
    }
    case WM_DESTROY:
    {
      PostQuitMessage(0);

DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  MSG msg;
  PeekMessage(&msg, NULL, WM_USER, WM_USER, PM_NOREMOVE);

  HANDLE hEvent = OpenEvent(EVENT_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, EVENT_NAME);

  if (hEvent != NULL)
  {
    SetEvent(hEvent);
  }
  CloseHandle(hEvent);

  while (GetMessage(&msg, NULL, 0, 0))
  {
    switch (msg.message)
    {
      case T_MESSAGE:
      {
        // TO DO
        // add some message processing here
        MessageBox(NULL, _T("Hi.\nI've just received a message."),
_T("Thread"), MB_OK);
        break;
      }
      case T_ENDTASK:
      {
        // main thread is exiting
        // return immediately
        return 0L;
      }
    }
  }
  return 0L;
}

61pipe_server.cpp — named-pipe server with per-client threadsbook pp. 162–164 · PDF pp. 177–179▼
Verbatim listing from the PDF
#include <windows.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <tchar.h>

#define BUFFER_SIZE 4096

DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter);

int _tmain(void)
{
  LPTSTR szPipename = _T("\\\\.\\pipe\\basicMPI");

  while (TRUE)
  {
    _tprintf(_T("basicMPI: waiting client connection\n"));

  HANDLE hPipe = CreateNamedPipe(szPipename, PIPE_ACCESS_DUPLEX,
    PIPE_WAIT | PIPE_READMODE_MESSAGE | PIPE_TYPE_MESSAGE,
    PIPE_UNLIMITED_INSTANCES, BUFFER_SIZE, BUFFER_SIZE, 0,
    NULL);

    if (hPipe == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE)
    {
      _tprintf(_T("CreateNamedPipe failed! Error code: [%u]\n"),
GetLastError());
      return 2;
    }

    if (ConnectNamedPipe(hPipe, NULL))
    {

      _tprintf(_T("Connection succeeded.\n"));

     HANDLE hThread = CreateThread(NULL, 0,
      (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)StartAddress, hPipe, 0, NULL);

      CloseHandle(hThread);
    }
  }

  return 0;
}

DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  HANDLE hPipe = (HANDLE)lpParameter;

  PTCHAR szRequest = (PTCHAR)HeapAlloc(GetProcessHeap(), 0,
    BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(TCHAR));
  PTCHAR szReply = (PTCHAR)HeapAlloc(GetProcessHeap(), 0,
    BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(TCHAR));
  DWORD dwBytesRead = 0;
  DWORD dwReplyBytes = 0;
  DWORD dwBytesWritten = 0;

  _tprintf(_T("Waiting messages.\n"));

  if (!ReadFile(hPipe, szRequest, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(TCHAR),
&dwBytesRead, NULL))
  {
    _tprintf(_T("ReadFile failed! Error code: [%u]\n"),
GetLastError());
    return 2L;
  }

  // do some processing

  _tprintf(_T("Client request:\"%s\"\n"), szRequest);

  _tcscpy_s(szReply, BUFFER_SIZE,
    _T("default answer from server"));

  dwReplyBytes = (_tcslen(szReply) + 1) * sizeof(TCHAR);

  if (!WriteFile(hPipe, szReply, dwReplyBytes, &dwBytesWritten,
NULL))
  {

    _tprintf(_T("WriteFile failed! Error code: [%u]"),
GetLastError());
    return 2L;
  }

  FlushFileBuffers(hPipe);
  DisconnectNamedPipe(hPipe);
  CloseHandle(hPipe);

  HeapFree(GetProcessHeap(), 0, szRequest);
  HeapFree(GetProcessHeap(), 0, szReply);

  _tprintf(_T("Success.\n"));

  return 0L;
}

#include <windows.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <tchar.h>

#define BUFFER_SIZE 4096

int _tmain(void)
{
  TCHAR szBuffer[BUFFER_SIZE];
  DWORD dwRead = 0;
  DWORD dwWritten = 0;
  DWORD dwMode = PIPE_READMODE_MESSAGE;
  LPTSTR szPipename = _T("\\\\.\\pipe\\basicMPI");
  LPTSTR szMessage = _T("Message from client.");
  DWORD dwToWrite = _tcslen(szMessage) * sizeof(TCHAR);

  HANDLE hPipe = CreateFile(szPipename, GENERIC_READ |
    GENERIC_WRITE, 0, NULL, OPEN_EXISTING, 0, NULL);

  WaitNamedPipe(szPipename, INFINITE);

  SetNamedPipeHandleState(hPipe, &dwMode, NULL, NULL);

  if (!WriteFile(hPipe, szMessage, dwToWrite, &dwWritten, NULL))

  {
    _tprintf(_T("WriteFile failed! Error code: [%u]\n"),
GetLastError());
    return -1;
  }

  _tprintf(
    _T("Message sent to server, receiving reply as follows:\n"));

  while (ReadFile(hPipe, szBuffer, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(TCHAR),
&dwRead, NULL) && GetLastError() != ERROR_MORE_DATA)
  {
    _tprintf(_T("%s"), szBuffer);
  }

  _tprintf(_T("\nSuccess!\nPress ENTER to exit."));
  scanf_s("%c", szBuffer);

  CloseHandle(hPipe);

  return 0;
}

28 Chapter 5 — Thread Synchronization and Concurrent Operations

The longest chapter in the book so far. It first clears up what concurrency can and cannot do on one core, explains Windows priorities and the dispatcher's thread states, and then solves the same problem five ways — with a mutex, a semaphore, an event, a critical section, and finally pipes between separate processes.

CORE TRUTH

Threads ≠ extra cores

Splitting work across eight threads on a single core only adds scheduling and synchronisation overhead.

SCHEDULING

Priority and quantum

Base priority comes from the process; dynamic priority is a temporary boost the dispatcher grants for important events.

ONE PROBLEM

Five solutions

A coordinate file feeds a queue of linear-equation systems; workers dequeue and solve them under different synchronisation schemes.

DESIGN FIRST

Protect the right thing

Ask what is shared, where exclusive access is required, and whether the object must cross a process boundary.

Chapter scope: book pp. 167–232 (PDF pp. 182–247), eight topics and 15 code listings — the biggest code appendix on this page.

30 Chapter 5: detailed summary

Pseudoparallelism — why more threads can be slower

  • Splitting a sum of x iterations between two threads does not halve the time on a single core: only one thread executes at any instant, and the OS must schedule both.
  • Eight threads on one core make things worse — extra thread creation, division overhead and waiting on synchronisation all add cost. Threads help when tasks block (input, I/O, remote calls) or when real cores are available.
  • Pseudoparallelism is still valuable: typing in Word while playing music, printing and burning a DVD feels simultaneous because the OS switches among threads very quickly.

Priority — controlling how often a thread runs

  • Priority controls how often a thread gets CPU time; synchronisation controls competition for shared resources and ordering. Interrupts outrank user processes; a thread's base priority comes from its owning process.
  • Code can move a thread's base priority only ±2 levels — a thread cannot be more important than its process. The OS can go further with dynamic priority: keystrokes, mouse clicks and disk data arrival temporarily boost the waiting thread.
  • Dynamic priority decays one step each time the thread receives its CPU time, settling back to base priority. The dispatcher picks the next thread by dynamic priority (Figure 1).
  • basic_priority.cpp keeps the UI thread at least one step above the drawing thread so the window stays responsive. On exit, an event is signalled and WaitForSingleObject joins the worker.
  • Warning: raising many priorities does not make a system faster — the OS then struggles to run its own tasks. Only a few processes (e.g. dwm.exe, taskmgr.exe) run above NORMAL.

The dispatcher object and scheduling

  • The dispatcher scans the ready queue from high to low priority, but not every thread is in that queue. Thread states: Ready, Standby, Running, Waiting, Transition and Terminated.
  • Loading a thread's context means restoring machine registers, kernel stack, environment block and user stack. If part of the context is swapped to disk, the thread sits in Transition until the system gathers it.
  • A thread runs for a quantum. A clock tick counter decreases until zero, then the dispatcher performs a context switch and selects the next thread.

The shared task: solve systems of two equations

  • Four variants use the same shape: a file of six coordinates per line (a1 b1 c1 a2 b2 c2) is loaded into a CQueue<QueueElement>; workers dequeue one system, solve it by Cramer's rule, update a progress bar and print the result.
  • QueueElement carries the six coefficients plus the HWNDs of the progress and result controls. The UI offers Browse and Start buttons, a label, a result area and a progress bar.
  • The design questions come first: how many threads, and what must be protected? The queue's Dequeue is the bottleneck — it must be exclusive.

Recipe 4 — Mutex

  • Query GetSystemInfo and start at most one thread per processor using sysInfo.dwNumberOfProcessors; SetThreadIdealProcessor hints where each should run (not a guarantee).
  • A named mutex protects queue.Dequeue(): one worker at a time takes a task. This is the "narrow gate" pattern applied to a concrete shared object.

Recipe 5 — Semaphore

  • Instead of creating N threads, create a semaphore with initial and maximum count equal to the CPU count. Workers wait on it with WaitForSingleObject(hSemaphore, INFINITE) and release with ReleaseSemaphore(hSemaphore, 1, NULL).
  • Same result, different technique — a reminder that the first correct solution is not the only one.

Recipe 6 — Event

  • The mutex still protects the queue; a named event is added so the user can abort. Each worker checks the event with WaitForSingleObject(hEvent, 10) (10 ms) at the top of its loop and exits if signalled.
  • This makes the application more responsive and shows how exclusive access and signalling usually appear together in multithreaded code.

Recipe 7 — Critical section

  • Critical section behaves like a mutex but is process-private and cheaper to create/manipulate. Since this application lives in one process, CRITICAL_SECTION plus EnterCriticalSection/LeaveCriticalSection is enough.
  • Choose between mutex and critical section by predicting use cases: cross-process sharing requires a mutex; single-process speed favours a critical section.

Recipe 8 — Pipes across process boundaries

  • The final version replaces worker threads with separate ClientProcess instances. Macros in main.h define the pipe, event, mutex and file-mapping names. The parent creates all four objects before the message loop and disposes of them afterwards.
  • A ListenerRoutine thread loops on ConnectNamedPipe, spawning a worker thread per client. The worker reads a request, takes the mutex, dequeues a QueueElement, writes it into shared file mapping (sized sizeof(QueueElement)), releases the mutex, and sends the coordinates through the pipe.
  • The client retries CreateFile with 0.1 s delays (many processes start at once, so ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE is likely), announces its PID with WriteFile, waits for a request like OK12345, then takes the mutex, reads coordinates from the mapping, solves the system and writes the result back.
  • Trade-off: processes are isolated by address space — safer by default — but slower to create and communicate through. Threads share everything, which is fast but demands careful synchronisation.
Chapter's closing advice: these techniques are "ground zero". Understand the process model, IPC and design before attempting complex concurrent systems.

  {
    return 1;
  }

  HANDLE hEvent = CreateEvent(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, RESET_EVENT);

    _T("Basic thread priority"), WS_OVERLAPPED | WS_CAPTION

  if (!hWnd)
  {

    | FF_MODERN, _T("Microsoft Sans Serif"));

}

LRESULT CALLBACK WindowProcedure(HWND hWnd, UINT uMsg, WPARAM
wParam, LPARAM lParam)
{
  switch (uMsg)
  {
    case WM_CREATE:
    {
      DWORD dwThreadId = 0;
      SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(),
        THREAD_PRIORITY_NORMAL);
      HANDLE hThread = CreateThread(NULL, 0,
        (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)StartAddress, hWnd,
         0, &dwThreadId);(LONG_PTR)dwThreadId);

      Sleep(100);
      CloseHandle(hThread);
      break;
    }
    case WM_CLOSE:
    {

      HANDLE hEvent = OpenEvent(EVENT_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE,
        RESET_EVENT);
      SetEvent(hEvent);
      DWORD dwThreadId = (DWORD) GetWindowLongPtr(hWnd,
        GWLP_USERDATA);
      HANDLE hThread = OpenThread(THREAD_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE,
        dwThreadId);

      WaitForSingleObject(hThread, INFINITE);
      CloseHandle(hThread);

      DestroyWindow(hWnd);
      break;
    }
    case WM_DESTROY:
    {
      PostQuitMessage(0);
      break;
    }
    default:
    {
      return DefWindowProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  HWND hWnd = (HWND)lpParameter;

  SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(),
    THREAD_PRIORITY_BELOW_NORMAL);
  HANDLE hEvent = OpenEvent(EVENT_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, RESET_EVENT);

  DWORD dwWaitResult(1);
  while (dwWaitResult != WAIT_OBJECT_0)
  {
    dwWaitResult = WaitForSingleObject(hEvent, 100);
    DrawProc(hWnd);
  }

  CloseHandle(hEvent);

  return 0L;
}

void DrawProc(HWND hWnd)
{
  int iTotal = 10;

  srand(GetNextSeed());

  HDC hDC = GetDC(hWnd);
  if (hDC)
  {
    for (int iCount = 0; iCount < iTotal; iCount++)
    {
      int iStartX = (int)(rand() % WINDOW_WIDTH);
      int iStopX = (int)(rand() % WINDOW_WIDTH);
      int iStartY = (int)(rand() % WINDOW_HEIGHT);
      int iStopY = (int)(rand() % WINDOW_HEIGHT);

      int iRed = rand() & 255;
      int iGreen = rand() & 255;
      int iBlue = rand() & 255;


      HANDLE hBrush = CreateSolidBrush(GetNearestColor(hDC,
RGB(iRed, iGreen, iBlue)));
      HANDLE hbrOld = SelectBrush(hDC, hBrush);

      Rectangle(hDC, min(iStartX, iStopX), max(iStartX, iStopX),
min(iStartY, iStopY), max(iStartY, iStopY));

      DeleteBrush(SelectBrush(hDC, hbrOld));
    }
    ReleaseDC(hWnd, hDC);
  }
}

unsigned GetNextSeed(void)
{
  static unsigned seed = (unsigned)time(NULL);
  return ++seed;
}

LRESULT CALLBACK WindowProcedure(HWND hWnd, UINT uMsg, WPARAM
wParam, LPARAM lParam)
{
  switch (uMsg)
  {
    case WM_DESTROY:
    {
      PostQuitMessage(0);
      break;
    }
    case WM_COMMAND:

    {
      switch (LOWORD(wParam))
      {
        case CONTROL_BROWSE:
        {
          if (!FileDialog(hWnd, szFilePath))
          {
            MessageBox(hWnd,
              _T("You must choose valid file path!"),
              _T("Error!"), MB_OK | MB_TOPMOST | MB_ICONERROR);
          }
          else
          {
            char szBuffer[MAX_PATH];
            wsprintfA(szBuffer,
              "\n File: %s Press \"Start\" now.",
              strrchr(szFilePath, '\\') + 1);

            SetWindowTextA(GetDlgItem(hWnd, CONTROL_TEXT),
szBuffer);
          }
          break;
        }
        case CONTROL_START:
        {
          if (!*szFilePath)
          {
            MessageBox(hWnd,
              _T("You must choose valid file path first!"),
              _T("Error!"), MB_OK | MB_TOPMOST | MB_ICONERROR);
            break;
          }

          ifstream infile(szFilePath);

          if (infile.is_open())
          {
            string line;
            while (std::getline(infile, line))
            {
              QueueElement* pQElement = new QueueElement();
              istringstream iss(line);

              if (!(iss >> pQElement->iA1 >> pQElement->iB1 >>
pQElement->iC1 >> pQElement->iA2 >> pQElement->iB2 >> pQElement-
>iC2))

              {
                break;
              }

              pQElement->hWndProgress = GetDlgItem(hWnd,
                CONTROL_PROGRESS);
              pQElement->hWndResult = GetDlgItem(hWnd,
                CONTROL_RESULT);

              queue.Enqueue(pQElement);
            }
            infile.close();

            SendMessage(GetDlgItem(hWnd, CONTROL_PROGRESS),
              PBM_SETRANGE, 0, MAKELPARAM(0, queue.Count()));

            SYSTEM_INFO sysInfo;
            GetSystemInfo(&sysInfo);
            for (DWORD dwIndex = 0; dwIndex <
              sysInfo.dwNumberOfProcessors; dwIndex++)
            {
              HANDLE hThread = CreateThread(NULL, 0,
                (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)StartAddress, &queue,
                0, NULL);
              SetThreadIdealProcessor(hThread, dwIndex);

              Sleep(100);
              CloseHandle(hThread);
            }
          }
          else
          {
            MessageBox(hWnd, _T("Cannot open file!"),
_T("Error!"), MB_OK | MB_TOPMOST | MB_ICONERROR);
          }
          break;
        }
      }
      break;
    }
    default:
    {
      return DefWindowProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
    }
  }

  return 0;
}

DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  // We'll solve the linear system using Cramer's rule:
  CQueue<QueueElement>* pQueue = (CQueue<QueueElement>*)
lpParameter;

  HANDLE hMutex = OpenMutex(MUTEX_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, szMutex);
  QueueElement* pQElement = NULL;

  while (true)
  {
    WaitForSingleObject(hMutex, INFINITE);

    pQElement = pQueue->Dequeue();

    ReleaseMutex(hMutex);

    if (pQElement == NULL)
    {
      break;
    }

    char szBuffer[1024];

    double dDeterminant = (pQElement->iA1 * pQElement->iB2) -
(pQElement->iB1 * pQElement->iA2);

    if (dDeterminant != 0)
    {
      double dX = ((pQElement->iC1 * pQElement->iB2) -
        (pQElement->iB1 * pQElement->iC2)) / dDeterminant;
      double dY = ((pQElement->iA1 * pQElement->iC2) -
        (pQElement->iC1 * pQElement->iA2)) / dDeterminant;

LRESULT CALLBACK WindowProcedure(HWND hWnd, UINT uMsg, WPARAM
wParam, LPARAM lParam)
{
  switch (uMsg)
  {
    case WM_DESTROY:
    {
      PostQuitMessage(0);
      break;
    }
    case WM_COMMAND:
    {
      switch (LOWORD(wParam))
      {
        case CONTROL_BROWSE:
        {
          if (!FileDialog(hWnd, szFilePath))
          {
            MessageBox(hWnd,
              _T("You must choose valid file path!"),
              _T("Error!"), MB_OK | MB_TOPMOST | MB_ICONERROR);
          }
          else
          {
            char szBuffer[MAX_PATH];
            wsprintfA(szBuffer,
              "\n File: %s Press \"Start\" now.",
              strrchr(szFilePath, '\\') + 1);

            SetWindowTextA(GetDlgItem(hWnd, CONTROL_TEXT),
szBuffer);
          }
          break;
        }
        case CONTROL_START:

        {
          if (!*szFilePath)
          {
            MessageBox(hWnd,
              _T("You must choose valid file path first!"),
              _T("Error!"), MB_OK | MB_TOPMOST | MB_ICONERROR);
            break;
          }

          ifstream infile(szFilePath);

          if (infile.is_open())
          {
            string line;
            while (std::getline(infile, line))
            {
              QueueElement* pQElement = new QueueElement();

              istringstream iss(line);

              if (!(iss >> pQElement->iA1 >> pQElement->iB1 >>
pQElement->iC1 >> pQElement->iA2 >> pQElement->iB2 >> pQElement-
>iC2))
              {
                break;
              }

              pQElement->hWndProgress = GetDlgItem(hWnd,
                CONTROL_PROGRESS);
              pQElement->hWndResult = GetDlgItem(hWnd,
                CONTROL_RESULT);

              queue.Enqueue(pQElement);
            }

            infile.close();

            SendMessage(GetDlgItem(hWnd, CONTROL_PROGRESS),
              PBM_SETRANGE, 0, MAKELPARAM(0, queue.Count()));

            int iCount = queue.Count();

            for (int iIndex = 0; iIndex < iCount; iIndex++)
            {
              HANDLE hThread = CreateThread(NULL, 0,
                (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)StartAddress, &queue,
                0, NULL);

              Sleep(100);
              CloseHandle(hThread);
            }
          }
          else
          {
            MessageBox(hWnd, _T("Cannot open file!"),
_T("Error!"), MB_OK | MB_TOPMOST | MB_ICONERROR);
          }
          break;
        }
      }
      break;
    }
    default:
    {
      return DefWindowProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  // We'll solve the linear system using Cramer's rule:
  CQueue<QueueElement>* pQueue = (CQueue<QueueElement>*)
lpParameter;

  HANDLE hMutex = OpenMutex(MUTEX_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, szMutex);
  HANDLE hSemaphore = OpenSemaphore(SEMAPHORE_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE,
szSemaphore);
  QueueElement* pQElement = NULL;

  while (true)
  {
    WaitForSingleObject(hSemaphore, INFINITE);
    ReleaseSemaphore(hSemaphore, 1, NULL);

    WaitForSingleObject(hMutex, INFINITE);
    pQElement = pQueue->Dequeue();
    ReleaseMutex(hMutex);

    if (pQElement == NULL)
    {
      break;

    }

    char szBuffer[1024];

    double dDeterminant = (pQElement->iA1 * pQElement->iB2) -
(pQElement->iB1 * pQElement->iA2);

    if (dDeterminant != 0)
    {
      double dX = ((pQElement->iC1 * pQElement->iB2) -
        (pQElement->iB1 * pQElement->iC2)) / dDeterminant;
      double dY = ((pQElement->iA1 * pQElement->iC2) -
        (pQElement->iC1 * pQElement->iA2)) / dDeterminant;

      sprintf_s(szBuffer, "  x = %8.4lf,\ty = %8.4lf\n", dX, dY);
    }
    else
    {
      sprintf_s(szBuffer, "  Determinant is zero.\n");
    }

    strcat_s(szResult, 4096, szBuffer);
    SetWindowTextA(pQElement->hWndResult, szResult);

    SendMessage(pQElement->hWndProgress, PBM_STEPIT, 0, 0);

    delete pQElement;

    Sleep(1000);
  }

  CloseHandle(hSemaphore);
  CloseHandle(hMutex);

  return 0L;
}

BOOL FileDialog(HWND hWnd, LPSTR szFileName)

  ofn.lpstrFile = szFile;

  ofn.nMaxFile = sizeof(szFile);
  ofn.lpstrFilter = "All\0*.*\0Text\0*.TXT\0";
  ofn.nFilterIndex = 1;
  ofn.lpstrFileTitle = NULL;
  ofn.nMaxFileTitle = 0;
  ofn.lpstrInitialDir = NULL;
  ofn.Flags = OFN_PATHMUSTEXIST | OFN_FILEMUSTEXIST;

  if (GetOpenFileNameA(&ofn) == TRUE)
  {
    strcpy_s(szFileName, MAX_PATH - 1, szFile);
    return TRUE;
  }

  return FALSE;
}

LRESULT CALLBACK WindowProcedure(HWND hWnd, UINT uMsg, WPARAM
wParam, LPARAM lParam)
{
  switch (uMsg)
  {

    case WM_DESTROY:
    {
      PostQuitMessage(0);
      break;
    }
    case WM_CLOSE:
    {
      HANDLE hEvent = OpenEvent(EVENT_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, szEvent);
      SetEvent(hEvent);
      CloseHandle(hEvent);

      DestroyWindow(hWnd);
      break;
    }
    case WM_COMMAND:
    {
      switch (LOWORD(wParam))
      {
        case CONTROL_BROWSE:
        {
          if (!FileDialog(hWnd, szFilePath))
          {
            MessageBox(hWnd,
              _T("You must choose valid file path!"),
              _T("Error!"), MB_OK | MB_TOPMOST | MB_ICONERROR);
          }
          else
          {
            char szBuffer[MAX_PATH];
            wsprintfA(szBuffer,
              "\n File: %s Press \"Start\" now.",
              strrchr(szFilePath, '\\') + 1);

            SetWindowTextA(GetDlgItem(hWnd, CONTROL_TEXT),
szBuffer);
          }
          break;
        }
        case CONTROL_START:
        {
          if (!*szFilePath)
          {
            MessageBox(hWnd,
              _T("You must choose valid file path first!"),
              _T("Error!"), MB_OK | MB_TOPMOST | MB_ICONERROR);

            break;
          }

          ifstream infile(szFilePath);

          if (infile.is_open())
          {
            string line;
            while (std::getline(infile, line))
            {
              QueueElement* pQElement = new QueueElement();
              istringstream iss(line);

              if (!(iss >> pQElement->iA1 >> pQElement->iB1 >>
pQElement->iC1 >> pQElement->iA2 >> pQElement->iB2 >> pQElement-
>iC2))
              {
                break;
              }

              pQElement->hWndProgress = GetDlgItem(hWnd,
                CONTROL_PROGRESS);
              pQElement->hWndResult = GetDlgItem(hWnd,
                CONTROL_RESULT);

              queue.Enqueue(pQElement);
            }

            infile.close();

            SendMessage(GetDlgItem(hWnd, CONTROL_PROGRESS),
              PBM_SETRANGE, 0, MAKELPARAM(0, queue.Count()));

            SYSTEM_INFO sysInfo;
            GetSystemInfo(&sysInfo);

            for (DWORD dwIndex = 0; dwIndex <
              sysInfo.dwNumberOfProcessors; dwIndex++)
            {
              HANDLE hThread = CreateThread(NULL, 0,
                (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)StartAddress, &queue,
                0, NULL);
              SetThreadIdealProcessor(hThread, dwIndex);

              Sleep(100);
              CloseHandle(hThread);
            }

          }
          else
          {
            MessageBox(hWnd, _T("Cannot open file!"),
_T("Error!"), MB_OK | MB_TOPMOST | MB_ICONERROR);
          }
          break;
        }
      }
      break;
    }
    default:
    {
      return DefWindowProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam);
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  // We'll solve the linear system using Cramer's rule:
  CQueue<QueueElement>* pQueue = (CQueue<QueueElement>*)
lpParameter;

  HANDLE hEvent = OpenEvent(EVENT_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, szEvent);
  QueueElement* pQElement = NULL;

  while (true)
  {
    DWORD dwStatus = WaitForSingleObject(hEvent, 10);

    if (dwStatus == WAIT_OBJECT_0)
    {
      break;
    }

    EnterCriticalSection(&criticalSection);

    pQElement = pQueue->Dequeue();

    LeaveCriticalSection(&criticalSection);

    if (pQElement == NULL)

    {
      break;
    }

    char szBuffer[1024];

    double dDeterminant = (pQElement->iA1 * pQElement->iB2) -
(pQElement->iB1 * pQElement->iA2);

    if (dDeterminant != 0)
    {
      double dX = ((pQElement->iC1 * pQElement->iB2) -
        (pQElement->iB1 * pQElement->iC2)) / dDeterminant;
      double dY = ((pQElement->iA1 * pQElement->iC2) -
        (pQElement->iC1 * pQElement->iA2)) / dDeterminant;

      sprintf_s(szBuffer, "  x = %8.4lf,\ty = %8.4lf\n", dX, dY);
    }
    else
    {
      sprintf_s(szBuffer, "  Determinant is zero.\n");
    }

    strcat_s(szResult, 4096, szBuffer);
    SetWindowTextA(pQElement->hWndResult, szResult);

    SendMessage(pQElement->hWndProgress, PBM_STEPIT, 0, 0);
    delete pQElement;

    Sleep(1000);
  }

  CloseHandle(hEvent);

  return 0L;
}

BOOL FileDialog(HWND hWnd, LPSTR szFileName)
{
  OPENFILENAMEA ofn;

  char szFile[MAX_PATH];

  ZeroMemory(&ofn, sizeof(ofn));

  ofn.lStructSize = sizeof(ofn);

  ofn.hwndOwner = hWnd;
  ofn.lpstrFile = szFile;
   ofn.lpstrFile[0] = '\0';
  ofn.nMaxFile = sizeof(szFile);
  ofn.lpstrFilter = "All\0*.*\0Text\0*.TXT\0";
  ofn.nFilterIndex = 1;
  ofn.lpstrFileTitle = NULL;
  ofn.nMaxFileTitle = 0;
  ofn.lpstrInitialDir = NULL;
  ofn.Flags = OFN_PATHMUSTEXIST | OFN_FILEMUSTEXIST;

  if (GetOpenFileNameA(&ofn) == TRUE)
  {
    strcpy_s(szFileName, MAX_PATH - 1, szFile);
    return TRUE;
  }

  return FALSE;
}

DWORD WINAPI ListenerRoutine(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  void** lpParameters = (void**)lpParameter;
  HWND hWndProgress = (HWND)lpParameters[0];
  HWND hWndResult = (HWND)lpParameters[1];

  HANDLE hEvent = OpenEvent(EVENT_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, EVENT_NAME);

  while (TRUE)
  {
    DWORD dwStatus = WaitForSingleObject(hEvent, INFINITE);
    if (dwStatus == WAIT_OBJECT_0)
    {
      break;
    }

    HANDLE hPipe = CreateNamedPipe(PIPE_NAME, PIPE_ACCESS_DUPLEX,
PIPE_WAIT | PIPE_READMODE_MESSAGE
      | PIPE_TYPE_MESSAGE, PIPE_UNLIMITED_INSTANCES, BUFFER_SIZE,
BUFFER_SIZE, 0, NULL);
    if (hPipe == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE)
    {
      char szBuffer[MAX_PATH];
      wsprintfA(szBuffer, "  Error: [%u]\n", GetLastError());

      SetWindowTextA(hWndResult, szBuffer);

      return 2L;
    }

    if (ConnectNamedPipe(hPipe, NULL))
    {
      void* params[2] = { hPipe, hWndResult };
      HANDLE hThread = CreateThread(NULL, 0,
        (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)StartAddress, params, 0, NULL);
      Sleep(100);
      CloseHandle(hThread);
    }

    SendMessage(hWndProgress, PBM_STEPIT, 0, 0);
  }

  CloseHandle(hEvent);
  return 0L;
}

DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  void** lpParameters = (void**)lpParameter;
  HANDLE hPipe = (HANDLE)lpParameters[0];
  HWND hWndResult = (HWND)lpParameters[1];

  char* szRequest = (char*)HeapAlloc(GetProcessHeap(), 0,
    BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(char));
  char* szReply = (char*)HeapAlloc(GetProcessHeap(), 0,
    BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(char));

  DWORD dwBytesRead = 0;
  DWORD dwReplyBytes = 0;
  DWORD dwBytesWritten = 0;

  memset(szRequest, 0, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(char));
  memset(szReply, 0, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(char));

  if (!ReadFile(hPipe, szRequest, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(char),
&dwBytesRead, NULL))
  {
    return 2L;
  }

  char szBuffer[1024] = { 0 };

  wsprintfA(szBuffer, "  PID: [%s] connected.\n", szRequest);
  strcat_s(szResult, szBuffer);
  SetWindowTextA(hWndResult, szResult);

  HANDLE hMutex = OpenMutex(MUTEX_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE, MUTEX_NAME);

  WaitForSingleObject(hMutex, INFINITE);

  QueueElement* pQElement = (QueueElement*)queue.Dequeue();

  HANDLE hMapping = OpenFileMapping(FILE_MAP_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE,
MAPPING_NAME);
  QueueElement* pMapping = (QueueElement*)MapViewOfFile(hMapping,
FILE_MAP_ALL_ACCESS, 0, 0, 0);

  memcpy(pMapping, pQElement, sizeof(QueueElement));

  UnmapViewOfFile(pMapping);
  CloseHandle(hMapping);

  ReleaseMutex(hMutex);
  CloseHandle(hMutex);

  sprintf_s(szReply, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(char), "OK%s",
szRequest);
  dwReplyBytes = (DWORD)((strlen(szReply) + 1) * sizeof(char));

  if (!WriteFile(hPipe, szReply, dwReplyBytes, &dwBytesWritten,
NULL))
  {
    return 2L;
  }

  memset(szRequest, 0, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(char));

  if (!ReadFile(hPipe, szRequest, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(char),
&dwBytesRead, NULL))
  {
    return 2L;
  }

  wsprintfA(szBuffer, "%s", szRequest);
  strcat_s(szResult, szBuffer);

  SetWindowTextA(hWndResult, szResult);

  delete pQElement;

  FlushFileBuffers(hPipe);
  DisconnectNamedPipe(hPipe);
  CloseHandle(hPipe);
  HeapFree(GetProcessHeap(), 0, szRequest);
  HeapFree(GetProcessHeap(), 0, szReply);

  return 0L;
}

BOOL FileDialog(HWND hWnd, LPSTR szFileName)
{
  OPENFILENAMEA ofn;

  char szFile[MAX_PATH];

  ZeroMemory(&ofn, sizeof(ofn));

  ofn.lStructSize = sizeof(ofn);
  ofn.hwndOwner = hWnd;
  ofn.lpstrFile = szFile;
  ofn.lpstrFile[0] = '\0';
  ofn.nMaxFile = sizeof(szFile);
  ofn.lpstrFilter = "All\0*.*\0Text\0*.TXT\0";
  ofn.nFilterIndex = 1;
  ofn.lpstrFileTitle = NULL;
  ofn.nMaxFileTitle = 0;
  ofn.lpstrInitialDir = NULL;
  ofn.Flags = OFN_PATHMUSTEXIST | OFN_FILEMUSTEXIST;

  if (GetOpenFileNameA(&ofn) == TRUE)
  {
    strcpy_s(szFileName, MAX_PATH - 1, szFile);
    return TRUE;
  }

  return FALSE;
}

BOOL StartProcess(HWND hWndResult)

{
  STARTUPINFO startupInfo = { 0 };
  PROCESS_INFORMATION processInformation = { 0 };

  BOOL bSuccess = CreateProcess(
    _T("..\\x64\\Debug\\ClientProcess.exe"), NULL, NULL, NULL,
    FALSE, 0, NULL, NULL, &startupInfo,  &processInformation);

  if (!bSuccess)
  {
    char szBuffer[MAX_PATH];
    wsprintfA(szBuffer, "  Process creation fails: [%u]\n",
GetLastError());

    SetWindowTextA(hWndResult, szBuffer);
  }

  return bSuccess;
}
78ClientProcess/main.cpp — solving an equation via the pipebook pp. 227–230 · PDF pp. 242–245▼
Verbatim listing from the PDF
#pragma once

#include "..\concurrent_operations5\main.h"

int _tmain(void)
{
  char szBuffer[BUFFER_SIZE];
  DWORD dwRead = 0;
  DWORD dwWritten = 0;
  DWORD dwMode = PIPE_READMODE_MESSAGE;

  char szMessage[1024] = { 0 };
  wsprintfA(szMessage, "%u", GetCurrentProcessId());

  DWORD dwToWrite = (DWORD)(strlen(szMessage) * sizeof(char));

  HANDLE hPipe = NULL;

  while (true)

  {
    hPipe = CreateFile(PIPE_NAME, GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE, 0,
NULL, OPEN_EXISTING, 0, NULL);
    if (hPipe != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE)
    {
      WaitNamedPipe(PIPE_NAME, INFINITE);
      SetNamedPipeHandleState(hPipe, &dwMode, NULL, NULL);
      break;
    }

    Sleep(100);
  }

  if (!WriteFile(hPipe, szMessage, dwToWrite, &dwWritten, NULL))
  {
    printf("Error: [%u]\n", GetLastError());
    return system("pause");
  }

  printf("Request sent.\nReceiving task:\n");
  char szResult[1024] = { 0 };

  while (ReadFile(hPipe, szBuffer, BUFFER_SIZE * sizeof(char),
&dwRead, NULL) && GetLastError() != ERROR_MORE_DATA)
  {
    if (szBuffer[0] == 'O' && szBuffer[1] == 'K' && ((DWORD)
strtol(szBuffer + 2, NULL, 10) == GetCurrentProcessId()))
    {
      printf("Client process: [%s]\n", szBuffer + 2);

      HANDLE hMutex = OpenMutex(MUTEX_ALL_ACCESS,
        FALSE, MUTEX_NAME);
      WaitForSingleObject(hMutex, INFINITE);

      HANDLE hMapping = OpenFileMapping(FILE_MAP_ALL_ACCESS,
FALSE, MAPPING_NAME);
      QueueElement* pMapping = (QueueElement*)
MapViewOfFile(hMapping, FILE_MAP_ALL_ACCESS, 0, 0, 0);

      if (pMapping != 0)
      {
        if (CalculateCramer(pMapping, szResult))
        {

          dwToWrite = (DWORD)(strlen(szResult) * sizeof(char));

          if (!WriteFile(hPipe, szResult, dwToWrite, &dwWritten,
NULL))
          {
            printf("Error: [%u]\n", GetLastError());
            break;
          }
          else
          {
            printf("Result: %s\n", szResult);
          }
        }
      }

      UnmapViewOfFile(pMapping);
      CloseHandle(hMapping);

      ReleaseMutex(hMutex);
      CloseHandle(hMutex);
    }
    else
    {
      printf("Error in connection [%u]\n", GetLastError());
    }
  }

  printf("\nSuccess!\nPress ENTER to exit.");
  scanf_s("%c", szBuffer);

  CloseHandle(hPipe);
  return 0;
}

bool CalculateCramer(QueueElement* pQElement, char* szResult)
{
  // We'll solve the linear system using Cramer's rule:
  double dDeterminant = (pQElement->iA1 * pQElement->iB2) -
(pQElement->iB1 * pQElement->iA2);
  if (dDeterminant != 0)
  {
    double dX = ((pQElement->iC1 * pQElement->iB2) -
      (pQElement->iB1 * pQElement->iC2)) / dDeterminant;

    double dY = ((pQElement->iA1 * pQElement->iC2) -
      (pQElement->iC1 * pQElement->iA2)) / dDeterminant;
    sprintf_s(szResult, strlen(szResult) - 1,
      " x = %8.4lf,\ty = %8.4lf\n", dX, dY);
  }
  else
  {
    sprintf_s(szResult, strlen(szResult) - 1,
      " Determinant is zero.\n");
  }

  return true;
}

35 Chapter 6 — Threads in the .NET Framework

The book steps out of native Win32 into the CLR. The chapter is deliberately practical: the same factorial-and-progress-bar program is rebuilt ten times, each rebuild introducing one more .NET idea — a task, a foreground thread, a lock, an event, an EAP event, a BackgroundWorker, cancellation, memory fences, Wait/Pulse, and finally a Barrier.

01 / RUNTIME

Managed vs native

Native C++ compiles straight to machine code on the HAL. C++/CLI compiles to MSIL, which the CLR checks and runs with a garbage collector.

02 / UNIT OF WORK

Task before Thread

A Task is queued work scheduled over a ThreadPool with work-stealing; a Thread gives explicit foreground/background control.

03 / UI RULE

Only the owner touches a control

Cross-thread UI access throws. The worker asks the UI thread via Invoke (synchronous) or BeginInvoke (asynchronous).

04 / PROGRESSION

From messages to barriers

PostMessage → Monitor lock → wait handle → event → EAP → BackgroundWorker → Wait/Pulse → Barrier: fewer lines, clearer intent.

Chapter scope: book pp. 233–308 (PDF pp. 248–323), thirteen topics, one figure and 35 code listings — the final and largest code appendix on this page.

37 Chapter 6: detailed summary

Managed versus unmanaged code — the trade-off

  • Unmanaged code is compiled directly into machine language and runs on the HAL: fast, low-level, and completely under programmer control. All earlier chapters used this approach.
  • Managed code is compiled to MSIL and executed by the CLR. Static type checking, runtime checks and a garbage collector come for free — but execution is slower and you can only do what the framework exposes.
  • The book's rule of thumb: native C++ (even assembly) for a nuclear power plant controller; .NET for a DVD rental UI that must look good and be finished quickly.
  • The syntax mirrors the two worlds: new/*/& allocate and reference unmanaged memory, while gcnew/^/% use the CLR heap, managed handles and managed references. GC reclaims the latter; addresses may move.

How .NET threading works — Task first

  • Thread lives in System::Threading; Task and its helpers live in System::Threading::Tasks. A Task abstracts concurrent work, while the CLR schedules it onto threads from the ThreadPool.
  • Creating a Task adds work to a queue; an available thread takes it. The pool uses work-stealing: simple work runs inline, complex work is split and idle threads on other cores steal sub-tasks, then results are merged.
  • The book recommends Task over a fixed number of Threads: hard-coding thread counts does not scale, can exceed core count and makes the UI unresponsive. (Thread is not available for Windows Store apps; Task is.)
  • The first CLRApplication example computes 25! on a Task while the main thread owns the UI. The worker may not touch the progress bar it did not create — it builds delegates and calls form->BeginInvoke(action) to have the UI thread do it.
  • _tWinMain sets [STAThreadAttribute] for COM-friendly UI, enables visual styles, and calls Application::Run(gcnew MyForm()).

Foreground and background threads

  • Foreground threads keep an application alive as long as they run. Background threads are killed automatically once the last foreground thread ends.
  • Thread objects are foreground by default; Task work runs in the background. Use a foreground Thread when the work must finish even if the user tries to close the window; use Task when closing the app should simply stop it.
  • The same Thread can behave as background with one line: thread->IsBackground = true; before Start().

Blocking, locks and the deadlock illustration

  • Blocking primitives: Thread::Sleep suspends for a time, Thread::Join waits for termination, and Task::Wait waits for completion — all preferable to a busy spin loop.
  • The CLRApplication3 version asks the user "calculate again?" by posting a custom END_TASK window message from the worker, overriding WndProc in the form. It needs User32.lib, which is implicit in native projects but must be added explicitly in CLR.
  • While waiting for the answer, the worker sleeps one second per iteration. The chapter calls this primitive and shows the .NET alternatives next.
  • CLRApplication4 adds a small RAII Lock class: its constructor calls Monitor::Enter(lockObject), its destructor calls Monitor::Exit. Creating and deleting the guard around each read/write of bContinue makes the shared flag safe. C# has a lock keyword; C++/CLI does not, hence the helper class.
  • A deadlock is mutual waiting: the traffic-jam figure below shows the classic four-way standoff. Here it could happen if the worker is suspended while holding the flag's lock. Detection and recovery are deferred to Chapter 8.

Thread safety and wait handles

  • In .NET, static members are thread-safe; instance members are not. Two threads enumerating the same List<int> each get their own enumerator, which is safe as long as nobody mutates the list.
  • initonly gives safe concurrent reads, illustrated by SafeValue::iValue being read by two Tasks.
  • Locks cost waiting time and can deadlock, so design the data sharing first. ManualResetEventSlim replaces the shared flag and polling: the worker calls Reset() then Wait(); the UI calls Set() when the user answers. With roughly 40 ns overhead it is ideal for short waits inside one process; for long waits it behaves like a normal ManualResetEvent.

Event-based asynchronous pattern and BackgroundWorker

  • EAP means the class creates and manages the worker for you: call WebClient::DownloadDataAsync, subscribe DownloadDataCompleted, and the handler runs on completion with the result in e->Result.
  • The factorial example imitates this with a static EndTaskEvent instead of a window message — it therefore also works in a console program with no message queue. The price: every UI change inside the event handler must still be marshalled with BeginInvoke because the event fires on the worker thread.
  • BackgroundWorker (in System::ComponentModel) is the general-purpose EAP implementation. Set WorkerReportsProgress, wire DoWork, ProgressChanged and RunWorkerCompleted, then call RunWorkerAsync. ReportProgress(i) raises the progress event and the completion event carries e->Result — no manual delegates for controls.
  • Unlike the sealed Thread, BackgroundWorker can be subclassed; override OnDoWork to carry extra state (the book's example is a weather prediction with many fields).

Interrupting, aborting and cancelling safely

  • Thread::Interrupt only throws ThreadInterruptedException when the target blocks (or the next time it blocks) — it may appear to do nothing on a running thread.
  • Thread::Abort works on non-blocked threads and throws ThreadAbortException, but both forced methods are unsafe: unmanaged code continues until the next managed statement, and you cannot fully predict the state you leave behind.
  • The recommended path is cooperative cancellation: set WorkerSupportsCancellation = true, call CancelAsync() from the closing form, and check worker->CancellationPending inside the loop to return cleanly.
  • Task::ContinueWith attaches a follow-up task that uses the first task's result. WaitAll and WaitAny are the managed cousins of the native wait APIs.

Non-blocking synchronization — fences and volatile

  • The compiler and CLR may reorder statements or cache reads/writes for optimisation. In the TestClass example, GetMethod can observe bState == true but still print iValue == 0.
  • Thread::MemoryBarrier() creates a full fence (~10 ns) around the flag: writes before it cannot move after, reads after it cannot move before.
  • Declaring the flag volatile gives cheaper half fences: an acquire fence on each read and a release fence on each write, leaving more room for optimisation.

Wait/Pulse and the Barrier class

  • Monitor::Wait and Monitor::Pulse/PulseAll suspend and wake a thread without spinning, but must be called while holding a lock. The worker waits on syncHandle, the UI thread pulses it after the user answers, and execution continues. A pulse costs about 100 ns versus ~400 ns to set an event handle.
  • A Barrier coordinates phases: create it with N participants, each calls SignalAndWait(), the counter drops, and only when it reaches zero are all tasks released. AddParticipant, RemoveParticipant, ParticipantCount and ParticipantRemaining manage the group.
  • The post-phase delegate passed to the constructor runs while all tasks are still paused — perfect for drawing the finished graph in CLRBarrier, where Parallel::Invoke runs two halves of one symmetric plot and EndTask paints the bitmap.
Chapter's closing advice: all these constructs are useful, but no single one fits every task. Understand the trade-offs, then choose deliberately before coding.

#pragma once
namespace CLRApplication
{
  using namespace System;
  using namespace System::Collections;
  using namespace System::Windows::Forms;
  using namespace System::Drawing;
  using namespace System::Threading::Tasks;

  public ref class MyForm : public Form
  {
  public:
    MyForm(void)
    {

      InitializeComponent();
      this->Load += gcnew System::EventHandler(this,
&MyForm::Form_OnLoad);
    }
  protected:
    ~MyForm()
    {
      if (components)
      {
        delete components;
      }
    }
  private:
    System::ComponentModel::Container ^components;
    Label^ label;
    ProgressBar^ progress;
    static const int N = 25;

    System::Void Form_OnLoad(System::Object^  sender,
System::EventArgs^  e)
    {
      InitializeApp();
    }

    System::Void InitializeApp(void)
    {
      label = gcnew Label();
      label->Location = Point(2, 25);

      progress = gcnew ProgressBar();
      progress->Location = Point(2, 235);
      progress->Width = 280;
      progress->Height = 25;
      progress->Step = 1;
      progress->Maximum = MyForm::N;
      progress->Value = 0;

      this->Controls->Add(label);
      this->Controls->Add(progress);

      Task^ task = gcnew Task(gcnew Action<Object^>
        (&MyForm::StartAddress), this);
      task->Start();
    }

    static System::Void StartAddress(Object^ parameter)

    {
      MyForm^ form = (MyForm^)parameter;

      UpdateProgressBarDelegate^ action =
        gcnew UpdateProgressBarDelegate(form,
        &MyForm::UpdateProgressBar);
      __int64 iResult = 1;

      for (int iIndex = 1;
        iIndex <= MyForm::N; iIndex++)
      {
        iResult *= iIndex;
        form->BeginInvoke(action);

        System::Threading::Thread::Sleep(100);
      }

      UpdateLabelTextDelegate^ textAction =
        gcnew UpdateLabelTextDelegate(form,
        &MyForm::UpdateLabelText);
      form->BeginInvoke(textAction, L"Result: "
        + Convert::ToString(iResult));
    }

    delegate void UpdateProgressBarDelegate(void);

    System::Void UpdateProgressBar(void)
    {
      progress->PerformStep();
    }

    delegate void UpdateLabelTextDelegate(String^ szText);

    System::Void UpdateLabelText(String^ szText)
    {
      label->AutoSize = false;
      label->Text = szText;
      label->AutoSize = true;
    }

    /// </summary>

    {
      this->AutoScaleMode =
        System::Windows::Forms::AutoScaleMode::Font;
      this->Size = System::Drawing::Size(300, 300);
      this->Text = L"MyForm";
      this->Padding = System::Windows::Forms::Padding(0);
      this->AutoScaleMode =
        System::Windows::Forms::AutoScaleMode::Font;
    }
#pragma endregion
  };
}

#pragma once

#include <Windows.h>
#pragma comment ( lib, "User32.lib" )
#define END_TASK  WM_USER + 1

namespace CLRApplication3
{
  using namespace System;
  using namespace System::Windows::Forms;
  using namespace System::Drawing;
  using namespace System::Threading::Tasks;

  public ref class MyForm : public Form
  {
  public:
    MyForm(void) : bContinue(true)
    {
      InitializeComponent();
      this->Load += gcnew System::EventHandler(this,
&MyForm::Form_OnLoad);
    }
  protected:
    ~MyForm()
    {
      if (components)
      {
        delete components;
      }
    }

    virtual void WndProc(Message% msg) override
    {
      switch (msg.Msg)
      {
        case END_TASK:
        {
          System::Windows::Forms::DialogResult^ dlgResult =
MessageBox::Show( L"Do you want to calculate again?", L"Question",
MessageBoxButtons::YesNo, MessageBoxIcon::Question);

          if (*dlgResult ==
            System::Windows::Forms::DialogResult::Yes)

          {
            bContinue = true;
            progress->Value = 0;
            label->Text = L"Calculating...";
          }

namespace CLRApplication10
{
  using namespace System;
  using namespace System::Threading;
  using namespace System::Threading::Tasks;
  using namespace System::Windows::Forms;
  using namespace System::Drawing;

  ref class Lock
  {
    Object^ lockObject;
  public:
    Lock(Object^ lock) : lockObject(lock)
    {
      Monitor::Enter(lockObject);
    }
  protected:
    ~Lock()
    {
      Monitor::Exit(lockObject);
    }
  };

  public ref class MyForm : public Form
  {
  public:
    MyForm(void) : syncHandle(gcnew Object())
    {
      InitializeComponent();
      this->Load += gcnew EventHandler(this,
        &MyForm::Form_OnLoad);
    }
  protected:
    ~MyForm()
    {
      if (components)
      {
        delete components;

      }
    }
    virtual void SetWait(void)
    {
      Lock^ lock = gcnew Lock(syncHandle);
      Monitor::Wait(syncHandle);
      delete lock;
    }
    virtual void SetPulse(void)
    {
      Lock^ lock = gcnew Lock(syncHandle);
      Monitor::Pulse(syncHandle);
      delete lock;
    }
  private:
    System::ComponentModel::Container ^components;
    Label^ label;
    ProgressBar^ progress;
    static const unsigned N = 25;
    initonly Object^ syncHandle;

    System::Void Form_OnLoad(Object^ sender, EventArgs^ e)
    {
      InitializeApp();
    }

    delegate void TaskCompletedDelegate(UInt64 uResult);
    void TaskCompleted(UInt64 uResult)
    {
      label->AutoSize = false;
      label->Text = L"Result: " + uResult;
      label->AutoSize = true;

      System::Windows::Forms::DialogResult^ dlgResult =
MessageBox::Show(L"Do you want to continue?", L"Question",
MessageBoxButtons::YesNo, MessageBoxIcon::Question);

      if (*dlgResult == System::Windows::Forms::DialogResult::Yes)
      {
        this->SetPulse();
        progress->Value = 0;
        label->Text = L"Calculating...";
      }
      else

      {
        this->Close();
      }
    }

    delegate void UpdateProgressBarDelegate(void);
    System::Void UpdateProgressBar(void)
    {
      progress->PerformStep();
    }

    System::Void InitializeApp(void)
    {
      label = gcnew Label();
      label->Location = Point(2, 25);

      progress = gcnew ProgressBar();
      progress->Location = Point(2, 235);
      progress->Width = 280;
      progress->Height = 25;
      progress->Step = 1;
      progress->Maximum = MyForm::N;
      progress->Value = 0;

      this->Controls->Add(label);
      this->Controls->Add(progress);

      Task^ task = gcnew Task(gcnew Action<Object^>
        (&MyForm::StartAddress), gcnew array<Object^>(2)
        { this, task });
      task->Start();
    }

    static System::Void StartAddress(Object^ parameter)
    {
      array<Object^>^ parameters = (array<Object^>^) parameter;

      MyForm^ form = (MyForm^)parameters[0];
      Task^ task = (Task^)parameters[1];

      TaskCompletedDelegate^ taskCompleted = gcnew
TaskCompletedDelegate(form, &MyForm::TaskCompleted);
      UpdateProgressBarDelegate^ updateProgressBar = gcnew
UpdateProgressBarDelegate(form, &MyForm::UpdateProgressBar);

      UInt64 uResult = 1;

      while (true)
      {
        uResult = 1;

        for (unsigned uIndex = 1; uIndex <= MyForm::N; uIndex++)
        {
          uResult *= uIndex;
          form->progress->BeginInvoke( updateProgressBar);

          Thread::Sleep(100);
        }

        form->BeginInvoke(taskCompleted, uResult);

        form->SetWait();
      }
    }

#pragma once

namespace CLRBarrier
{
  using namespace System;
  using namespace System::ComponentModel;
  using namespace System::Collections::Generic;
  using namespace System::Windows::Forms;
  using namespace System::Threading;
  using namespace System::Threading::Tasks;
  using namespace System::Drawing;

  public ref class MyForm : public Form
  {
  public:
    MyForm(void)
    {
      InitializeComponent();

      iWidth = 800;
      iHeight = 600;

      bitmapGraph = gcnew Bitmap(iWidth, iHeight);
      colorArray = gcnew array<Color>(iWidth * iHeight);

      color = Color::FromArgb(0, 0, 255);

      progress->Maximum = iWidth / 2;
    }
  protected:
    ~MyForm()

    {
      if (components)
      {
        delete components;
      }
    }
  private:
    System::Windows::Forms::GroupBox^  groupBox;
    System::Windows::Forms::Label^  status;
    System::Windows::Forms::ProgressBar^  progress;
    System::Windows::Forms::Button^  btnStart;
    System::Windows::Forms::PictureBox^  canvas;
    System::ComponentModel::Container ^components;

    int iWidth;
    int iHeight;
    array<Color>^ colorArray;
    Bitmap^ bitmapGraph;
    Barrier^ barrier;
    Color color;

    delegate void UpdateProgressDelegate(void);
    System::Void UpdateProgress(void)
    {
      progress->PerformStep();
    }

    delegate void SetCanvasDelegate(void);
    void SetCanvas(void)
    {
      canvas->BackColor = Color::Black;
      canvas->Image = bitmapGraph;
    }

    delegate void SetLabelTextDelegate(String^ szText);
    void SetLabelText(String^ szText)
    {
      status->Text = szText;
    }

    System::Void EndTask(Barrier^ b)
    {

      FillBitmap();

      SetLabelTextDelegate^ setLabelText = gcnew
SetLabelTextDelegate(this, &MyForm::SetLabelText);
      status->BeginInvoke(setLabelText, L"Done.");

      SetCanvasDelegate^ canvasDelegate = gcnew
SetCanvasDelegate(this, &MyForm::SetCanvas);
      canvas->BeginInvoke(canvasDelegate);
    }

    System::Void btnStart_Click(Object^ sender, EventArgs^  e)
    {
      status->Text = L"Calculating...";

      Action^ action = gcnew Action(this,
&MyForm::CalculateValues);

      barrier = gcnew Barrier(2, gcnew Action<Barrier^>(this,
&MyForm::EndTask));

      Tasks::Parallel::Invoke(action, action);
    }

    System::Void FillBitmap(void)
    {
      for (int iYPosition = 0; iYPosition < iHeight; iYPosition++)
      {
        for (int iXPosition = 0; iXPosition < iWidth;
iXPosition++)
        {
          bitmapGraph->SetPixel(iXPosition, iYPosition,
colorArray[(iXPosition + (iWidth * iYPosition))]);
        }
      }
    }

    System::Void CalculateValues(void)
    {
      int iLeft = iWidth / 2;
      int iArea = iLeft * iLeft;

      int iTop = iHeight / 2;

      UpdateProgressDelegate^ updateProgress = gcnew
UpdateProgressDelegate(this, &MyForm::UpdateProgress);

      for (int iXAxis = 0; iXAxis < iLeft; iXAxis++)
      {
        int iSurface = iXAxis * iXAxis;
        double dSquare = Math::Sqrt(iArea - iSurface);

        for (double dIndex = -dSquare; dIndex < dSquare; dIndex +=
3)
        {
          double dRadius = Math::Sqrt(iSurface + dIndex * dIndex)
/ iLeft;
          double dBottom = (dRadius - .96) * Math::Sin(32 *
dRadius);
          double dYAxis = dIndex / 3 + (dBottom * iTop);

          SetPixelValue(colorArray, (int) (-iXAxis + (iWidth /
2)), (int) (dYAxis + (iHeight / 2)));
          SetPixelValue(colorArray, (int) (iXAxis + (iWidth / 2)),
(int) (dYAxis + (iHeight / 2)));
        }

        progress->BeginInvoke(updateProgress);
      }

      barrier->SignalAndWait();
    }

    System::Void SetPixelValue(array<Color>^ graphArray, int
iXPos, int iYPos)
    {
      int iIndex = (iXPos + iYPos * iWidth);
      graphArray[iIndex] = color;
    }

42 Chapter 7 — Understanding Concurrent Code Design

This chapter changes the question from "which API do I call?" to "is this design correct, and is parallelism worth it at all?" It classifies concurrency bugs, builds one numerical program three times — sequential, hand-threaded, and OpenMP — and measures the gain instead of assuming it.

01 / BUGS

Correctness vs. liveness

Correctness bugs produce wrong answers; liveness bugs make the program stop producing answers at all.

02 / ORDER

Sequential first

Write and optimise the sequential algorithm, then transform it carefully. Parallelism added to a weak design only amplifies its flaws.

03 / BOUNDARY

Protect the whole region

Locking only half of a read-modify-write sequence still crashes; thread-local work plus one protected merge is better.

04 / MEASURE

Speed-up, not hope

I = T(S) / T(P). Compare I with the core count P; sublinear improvement is normal.

Chapter scope: book pp. 309–340 (PDF pp. 324–355), four topics, four figures and 27 code listings — the final appendix on this page.

44 Chapter 7: detailed summary

Correctness versus liveness

  • Correctness problems make a program produce wrong results. They are hard to catch because each thread follows a different path; a program may return correct answers many times before one bad interleaving appears.
  • Liveness problems make a program stop producing results — it hangs or becomes unresponsive rather than crashing. Deadlock is the chapter's main example.
  • Poorly designed parallel code can be slower than sequential code: rescheduling threads, fetching memory blocks, signalling objects and maintaining protection all cost CPU time.
  • Chapter 6 said "choose the right synchronisation object". Chapter 7 adds "choose the right design" — the object alone cannot repair a wrong execution flow.

Data races and inconsistent synchronisation

  • A data race occurs when several threads read and write a shared object without a defined order. The chapter's iValue = 5 example copies it into two thread-local variables at different times; without mutual exclusion the final value is unpredictable.
  • Protection must be consistent. The CLock wrapper calls CreateMutex with a name and waits in its constructor, then releases and closes in the destructor. If funcA uses _tmp_lock_01_ and funcB uses _tmp_lock_02_, they protect nothing relative to each other — both increment the same iValue concurrently.
  • Even read-only sharing can be dangerous when combined with writes elsewhere; classify each shared object before deciding what to protect.

Composite actions — lock the whole critical region

  • Removing the head of a singly linked list needs two statements: node == NULL then next = node->next. The first incorrect version protects only the assignment.
  • The interleaving figure shows why that fails: thread A checks the list is non-empty, is suspended, thread B checks the same thing, A removes the node, and B then dereferences a node that no longer exists — "APP CRASH".
  • The correct version takes the lock before the NULL check and releases it after the assignment. Fewer protected statements mean more concurrency, but you must include the entire logically atomic sequence.
  • Group critical points into small, heavily protected portions, then examine every use case before declaring the flow safe.

Deadlock in the bank transfer

  • CBankAccount::Transfer(a, b, amount) locks account A, then account B, adjusts both balances, and releases both locks. It looks correct.
  • With two opposite transfers — A→B and B→A — thread A acquires lock_1 on X and thread B acquires lock_2 on Y. Each then waits for the lock the other holds. The second timing figure shows both threads "WAIT FOREVER".
  • The event may be rare, but a concurrent design must rule it out, not merely hope it never happens. A common fix is to acquire locks in a consistent global order.

Design before code — Schwefel's function

  • The example computes Schwefel's function over an array of up to 100,000 random alleles in [-65.536, 65.536]: square the inner sum for each position, accumulate score, and track sum, minimum and best value.
  • CSchwefel is deliberately designed for extension: Evaluate and the destructor are virtual, one void* parameter is reserved for thread arguments, the copy constructor and assignment operator are disabled (a shallow copy would leave two objects pointing at one allele array), and ObjectName() is overridden by each derived class for the console output.
  • Initialize fills the array and computes the initial sum/min; Elapsed formats timings using a custom SYSTEMTIME subtraction operator built on SystemTimeToFileTime and FileTimeToSystemTime.
  • The entry point simply constructs CSchwefel(100000), calls Evaluate() and prints Elapsed(). Strong sequential code first; parallelism is added only afterwards.

From sequential to multi-threaded

  • CSchwefelMT derives from CSchwefel and overrides only Evaluate. It splits the array into ThreadNumber chunks, passes a ThreadParams structure to each CreateThread, waits with WaitForMultipleObjects, then closes handles.
  • The naive StartAddress updates Sum(), Min(), Score() and Best() directly from every thread. The third figure shows the harm: two CPUs both load dSum = 42.56 from address 4004, add different alleles, and write back one value — the other addition is lost.
  • The corrected version reads the shared values once under a mutex into thread-local dSum/dMin/dScore/dBest, performs the whole loop without locks, then takes the mutex again to merge the results. Protected boundaries, parallel middle — "safe and clean".
  • Putting the mutex inside the loop would serialise nearly all the work and defeat the purpose of parallelism.

OpenMP and measuring improvement

  • CSchwefelP uses the compiler's OpenMP support: #pragma omp parallel firstprivate(min) firstprivate(best) gives each thread its own copies of the extrema; #pragma omp for reduction(+: sum) reduction(+: score) nowait splits the loop and merges the sums safely; #pragma omp critical serialises the final comparison of min/best.
  • firstprivate initialises each private copy from the value before the region; reduction combines private results at the end under mutual exclusion; nowait removes the implicit barrier at the loop's end.
  • Improvement is I = T(S) / T(P). I < 1 is slowdown, I < P sublinear, I ~ P linear, and I > P superlinear (rare, sometimes possible when intermediate results are shared).
  • On an Intel i7-3820 with 8 logical cores: sequential 4057 ms, 8-thread CSchwefelMT 955 ms → I = 4.248; OpenMP 959 ms → I = 4.231. Both are sublinear — the normal result when synchronisation and communication exist.
  • A slowdown can also mean the code was poorly parallelised, had too many protection points, or the target hardware has fewer cores than the test machine. Measure before and after, on the hardware that matters.
Chapter's closing advice: plan from design to code in steps, decide whether parallelism actually helps, and let practice confirm the theory.

template class<T>
class CList<T>
{

  T* value;

template class<T>
T* CList::Pop( void )
{
  CList* node = next;
  if (node == NULL)
  {
    return 0;
  }

  CLock* lock = new CLock(_T("_tmp_lock_"));
  next = node->next;
  delete lock;

  return node->value;
}

  CLock* lock = new CLock(_T("_tmp_lock_"));

  CList* node = next;
  if (node == NULL)

  }

  next = node->next;
  delete lock;

}

class CBankAccount

dAmount);

TCHAR* CBankAccount::LockName(void)
{
  static int iCount = 0;
  static TCHAR szBuffer[16];
  wsprintf( szBuffer, _T("_lock_%d_"), ++iCount );
  return szBuffer;
}

void CBankAccount::Transfer(CBankAccount* a, CBankAccount* b, double
dAmount )
{
  CLock* outerLock = new CLock(a->szLock);
  if (dAmount < a->dBalance)
  {
    CLock* innerLock = new CLock(b->szLock);
    a->dBalance -= dAmount;
    b->dBalance += dAmount;
    delete innerLock;
  }
  delete outerLock;
}

#include "stdafx.h"

double CSchwefel::Evaluate(void* lpParameters)
{
  GetSystemTime(&stStart);

  for (unsigned i = 0; i < uSize; i++)
  {
    dSum += pdAllele[i];

    if (dMin > pdAllele[i])
    {
      dMin = pdAllele[i];
    }

    double dInnerSum = 0;

    for (unsigned j = 0; j < i; j++)
    {
      dInnerSum += pdAllele[j];
    }

    double dTmp = dInnerSum * dInnerSum;
    dScore += dTmp;

    if (i != 0 && dBest > dTmp)
    {
      dBest = dTmp;
    }
  }

  GetSystemTime(&stEnd);

  return dScore;
}

128SYSTEMTIME subtraction operatorbook pp. 321–322 · PDF pp. 336–337▼
Verbatim listing from the PDF
SYSTEMTIME operator - (const SYSTEMTIME& stFirst, const
SYSTEMTIME& stSecond)
{
  SYSTEMTIME stResult;
  FILETIME ftTime;

  ULARGE_INTEGER uLargeInteger;

  __int64 i64Right;
  __int64 i64Left;
  __int64 i64Result;

  SystemTimeToFileTime(&stFirst, &ftTime);
  uLargeInteger.LowPart = ftTime.dwLowDateTime;
  uLargeInteger.HighPart = ftTime.dwHighDateTime;
  i64Right = uLargeInteger.QuadPart;

  SystemTimeToFileTime(&stSecond, &ftTime);
  uLargeInteger.LowPart = ftTime.dwLowDateTime;
  uLargeInteger.HighPart = ftTime.dwHighDateTime;
  i64Left = uLargeInteger.QuadPart;

  i64Result = i64Right - i64Left;

  uLargeInteger.QuadPart = i64Result;
  ftTime.dwLowDateTime = uLargeInteger.LowPart;
  ftTime.dwHighDateTime = uLargeInteger.HighPart;
  FileTimeToSystemTime(&ftTime, &stResult);

  return stResult;
}

132CSchwefelMT::StartAddress — unsynchronised first attemptbook pp. 326–327 · PDF pp. 341–342▼
Verbatim listing from the PDF
#include "stdafx.h"

DWORD WINAPI CSchwefelMT::StartAddress(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  ThreadParams* params = (ThreadParams*)lpParameter;

  unsigned uChunk = ((unsigned)params->this_ptr->Size()) /
ThreadNumber;
  unsigned uMax = (params->uThreadIndex + 1) * uChunk;

  for (unsigned i = params->uThreadIndex * uChunk; i < uMax; i++)
  {
    params->this_ptr->Sum() += params->this_ptr->Allele(i);

    if (params->this_ptr->Min() > params->this_ptr->Allele(i))
    {
      params->this_ptr->Min() = params->this_ptr->Allele(i);
    }

    double dInnerSum = 0;

    for (unsigned j = 0; j < i; j++)
    {
      dInnerSum += params->this_ptr->Allele(j);
    }

    double dTmp = dInnerSum * dInnerSum;

    params->this_ptr->Score() += dTmp;

    if (i != 0 && params->this_ptr->Best() > dTmp)
    {
      params->this_ptr->Best() = dTmp;
    }
  }

  return 0L;
}
133CSchwefelMT::Evaluate — CreateThread + WaitForMultipleObjectsbook p. 327 · PDF p. 342▼
Verbatim listing from the PDF
double CSchwefelMT::Evaluate(void* lpParameters)
{
  HANDLE hThreads[ThreadNumber];
  ThreadParams params[ThreadNumber];

  GetSystemTime(&StartTime());

  for (unsigned uIndex = 0; uIndex < ThreadNumber; uIndex++)
  {
    params[uIndex] = { this, uIndex };
    hThreads[uIndex] = CreateThread(NULL, 0, (LPTHREAD_START_
ROUTINE)StartAddress, &params[uIndex], 0, NULL);
  }

  WaitForMultipleObjects(ThreadNumber, hThreads, TRUE, INFINITE);

  GetSystemTime(&EndTime());

  for (unsigned uIndex = 0; uIndex < ThreadNumber; uIndex++)
  {
    CloseHandle(hThreads[uIndex]);
  }

  return Score();
}

if (dMin < params->this_ptr->Min())

{
  params->this_ptr->Min() = dMin;
}
params->this_ptr->Score() = dScore;
if (dBest < params->this_ptr->Best())
{
  params->this_ptr->Best() = dBest;
}

ReleaseMutex(hMutex);
CloseHandle(hMutex);

return 0L;
}

138CSchwefelP.cpp — OpenMP parallel / reduction / criticalbook pp. 334–335 · PDF pp. 349–350▼
Verbatim listing from the PDF
#include "stdafx.h"

double CSchwefelP::Evaluate(void* lpParameters)
{
  GetSystemTime(&StartTime());

  double sum = 0;
  double score = 0;
  double min = DBL_MAX;
  double best = DBL_MAX;
  int iSize = (int)Size();

#pragma omp parallel firstprivate(min) firstprivate(best)
  {
#pragma omp for reduction(+: sum) reduction(+: score) nowait
    for (int i = 0; i < iSize; i++)
    {
      sum += Allele(i);

      if (min > Allele(i))
      {
        min = Allele(i);

      }

      double dInnerSum = 0;

      for (int j = 0; j < i; j++)
      {
        dInnerSum += Allele(j);
      }

      double dTmp = dInnerSum * dInnerSum;
      score += dTmp;

      if (i != 0 && best > dTmp)
      {
        best = dTmp;
      }
    }

#pragma omp critical
    {
      if (Best() > best)
      {
        Best() = best;
      }
      if (Min() > min)
      {
        Min() = min;
      }
    }
  }

  Sum() = sum;
  Score() = score;

  GetSystemTime(&EndTime());

  return Score();
}
