APPENDIX TO THIS PAGE — CHAPTER 8

49 Chapter 8 — Advanced Thread Management

The final chapter adds a management layer above threads. First a pool reuses a bounded set of workers; then the dispatcher becomes "smart" by wrapping every task in a worker/context pair and using Windows wait-chain APIs to detect deadlocks; finally a remote thread runs a DLL inside another process, where ordinary function addresses would be meaningless.

01 / MANAGER

One object owns the work

A manager creates tasks, schedules them, grants exclusive access, watches resources and destroys work cleanly.

02 / REUSE

Pool instead of churn

CThreadPool hands out CThread objects and caps them, avoiding create/destroy overhead for many small tasks.

03 / DETECTION

Worker + context thread

The worker waits for its context thread with a timeout, then posts MSG_ENDTASK; a separate ProblemSolver uses WCT to find cycles.

04 / INJECTION

Across process boundaries

CreateRemoteThread runs LoadLibraryA in calc.exe; a DLL and a file mapping carry the code and the results.

Chapter scope: book pp. 341–380 (PDF pp. 356–395), three topics, four figures and 20 code listings — the last appendix on this page.

50 Chapter 8: three topics at a glance

#TopicWhat you should take awayBook / PDF p.
1Using thread poolsA bounded list of reusable workers, dispatched by a manager instead of creating a thread per task.342 / 357
2Customizing the dispatcherWorker/context pairs, completion messages, and a WCT-based problem solver that detects and terminates deadlocks.354 / 369
3Using remote threadingInject a DLL into another process with CreateRemoteThread; share state via file mapping and events.371 / 386

51 Chapter 8: detailed summary

Why a manager object?

  • Complex programs need mechanisms above individual threads. The book points to the Windows Dispatcher (scheduling and synchronisation) and the Virtual Memory manager as examples of one root object responsible for managing many tasks.
  • Such a manager creates and destroys tasks, checks that resources are available, grants exclusive access, and ensures no two tasks perform invalid or unsynchronised operations.
  • With parallelism comes a thread hierarchy: some threads are more important and must supervise others. Design that hierarchy before writing the workers.

The basic thread pool

  • A pool is a list of worker threads available to execute tasks. It helps when an application would otherwise spawn a large number of short-lived threads — creation and destruction overhead dominates the actual work.
  • CThread wraps a start address, handle, thread ID and exit code. Its destructor terminates a still-running thread; Start calls CreateThread, StillAlive compares GetExitCodeThread with STILL_ACTIVE.
  • CThreadPool stores CList<CThread> and a maximum count (logical processors by default). RequestThread creates a new worker while below the cap; otherwise it polls every 100 ms until a worker finishes, removes it and inserts a replacement. WaitAll uses WaitForMultipleObjects with bWaitAll = TRUE.
  • The demo program creates twelve CBankAccount objects with random balances and submits five random transfers. CLock again guards two named mutexes, and the transfer returns 1 on success or 0 when funds are insufficient.
  • Limitation: a deadlock can still happen if two opposite transfers overlap exactly. Polling alone cannot detect it — which motivates the smarter dispatcher.

Custom dispatcher: worker and context thread

  • Rather than polling the list, completion now uses message passing: the first worker to finish posts MSG_ENDTASK to the dispatcher, which blocks in GetMessage and wakes only when a task is done.
  • Each pool item is a worker thread created with CREATE_SUSPENDED. Its StartAddress creates a second context thread that runs the user function, then waits at most MAX_WAIT_TIME (120 s, adjustable with SetMaxWaitTime), closes the context handle and posts the completion message carrying the worker ID.
  • If the context thread terminates or hangs, the worker notices through its exit status or timeout and can notify the dispatcher. This doubles the thread count per task but preserves the pool cap and gives fine-grained control.
  • CBankAccount::Transfer gains a deliberate Sleep(100) at the start so that opposite transfers reliably overlap and create the deadlock the problem solver must handle.

The ProblemSolver and Wait Chain Traversal

  • CThreadPool now includes Wct.h and links Advapi32.lib. It owns a hProblemSolver thread, a manual-reset hEvent for shutdown, the worker list and the cap.
  • The monitoring thread must be outside the pool — if it were a pool worker it could be blocked along with the pool. Each loop waits 10 ms on the exit event, then inspects every worker with StillAlive.
  • For each live worker it opens a Wait Chain Traversal session with OpenThreadWaitChainSession and calls GetThreadWaitChain on the context thread. A wait chain alternates threads and synchronisation objects; when the nodes form a cycle, the API sets IsCycle to TRUE.
  • On a detected cycle the solver calls TerminateThread on the context handle, prints "Error! Deadlock found! Thread: [id] terminated!", closes the WCT session, sleeps one second and keeps watching. The screenshot shows two accounts repeatedly transferring until a cycle is found and broken.
  • The destructor signals the event, waits up to MAX_WAIT_TIME for a clean exit, forcibly terminates the monitor only if needed, then closes handles, removes workers and clears the message queue.
  • The book names this scenario the Banker's algorithm (Edsger Dijkstra) and notes that the same pool-plus-solver pattern generalises to other deadlock-prone work.

Remote threading

  • Sometimes you must change behaviour in compiled code you cannot edit. A remote thread runs in another process's address space. Windows offers CreateRemoteThread, SetWindowsHookEx and the undocumented NtCreateThreadEx; the chapter uses the first.
  • A function address in your own process is useless in the target, so the thread's start address must be a system function: LoadLibraryA. Its argument — the absolute DLL path — is written into the target with VirtualAllocEx and WriteProcessMemory. The remote thread loads the DLL, and DllMain(DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH) runs your code in that process.
  • common.h shares the file-mapping and event names between the EXE and DLL. In the DLL, OpenFileMapping obtains a structure where it writes hInstance — the DLL handle the parent needs later for FreeLibrary.
  • The example changes the main-window title of calc.exe. EnumWindows visits top-level windows, GetWindowThreadProcessId matches the owning process, and IsMainWindow checks no owner plus IsWindowVisible; then SetWindowText changes the title and SetEvent tells the parent the job is done.
  • The parent starts calc.exe with CreateProcess, waits 500 ms for initialisation, calls RemoteLoadLibrary, waits on the event, maps the shared view, calls RemoteFreeLibrary with the reported handle, then closes handles. For an existing target, OpenProcess must request PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS or CreateRemoteThread will fail.
Book's closing advice: concurrency rests on operating systems, compilers, OOP, execution and runtime knowledge. Get the design right first, then practise — a lot.

DWORD WINAPI CBankAccount::Transfer(LPVOID lpParameter)
{
  CParameters* parameters = (CParameters*)lpParameter;

  CLock* outerLock = new CLock(parameters->fromAccount->szLock);

  if (parameters->dAmount < parameters->fromAccount->dBalance)
  {
    CLock* innerLock = new CLock(parameters->toAccount->szLock);
    parameters->fromAccount->dBalance -= parameters->dAmount;
    parameters->toAccount->dBalance += parameters->dAmount;
    delete innerLock;
    delete outerLock;

    if (parameters->bPrintOutput)
    {
      _tprintf_s(_T("%ws\n%ws\t\t%8.2lf\n%ws\t%8u\n%ws\t%8.2lf\
n%ws\t%8u\n%ws\t%8.2lf\n\n"),
        L"Transfer succeeded.",
        L"Amount:", parameters->dAmount,
        L"From account:", parameters->fromAccount->AccountID(),
        L"Balance:", parameters->fromAccount->Balance(),
        L"To account:", parameters->toAccount->AccountID(),
        L"Balance:", parameters->toAccount->Balance());
    }

    delete parameters;
    return 1;
  }
  delete outerLock;

  if (parameters->bPrintOutput)
  {
    _tprintf_s(_T("%ws\n%ws\t\t%8.2lf\n%ws\t%8u\n%ws\t%8.2lf\n%ws\
t%8u\n%ws\t%8.2lf\n%ws\n\n"),
      L"Transfer failed.",
      L"Amount:", parameters->dAmount,
      L"From account:", parameters->fromAccount->AccountID(),
      L"Balance:", parameters->fromAccount->Balance(),
      L"To account:", parameters->toAccount->AccountID(),
      L"Balance:", parameters->toAccount->Balance(),
      L"Not enough funds!");
  }

  delete parameters;
  return 0;
}

Verbatim listing from the PDF
#ifndef __THREADPOOL__
#define __THREADPOOL__

#include "main.h"
#include "CList.h"
#include "CThread.h"

class CThreadPool
{
public:
  CThreadPool();
  CThreadPool(unsigned uMaxThreads) : dwMaxCount(uMaxThreads),
threadList(new CList<CThread>()){ }
  ~CThreadPool(){ RemoveAll(); }
  DWORD Count(){ return threadList->Count(); }
  void RemoveThread(DWORD dwThreadId);
  void WaitAll();
  void RemoveAll();
  DWORD& MaxCount(){ return dwMaxCount; }
  void ReleaseThread(DWORD dwThreadId);
  CThread* RequestThread(LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE threadStart);
private:
  CList<CThread>* threadList;
  DWORD dwMaxCount;
};

CThreadPool::CThreadPool()
{
  SYSTEM_INFO sysInfo;
  GetSystemInfo(&sysInfo);
  dwMaxCount = sysInfo.dwNumberOfProcessors;

  threadList = new CList<CThread>();
}

void CThreadPool::RemoveThread(DWORD dwThreadId)
{

  CThread* thread = threadList->Find(CThread::GetThreadId,
dwThreadId);
  if (thread)
  {
    delete thread;
  }
}

void CThreadPool::WaitAll()
{
  HANDLE* hThreads = new HANDLE[threadList->Count()];
  CThread* thread = 0;

  for (unsigned uIndex = 0; uIndex < threadList->Count();
uIndex++)
  {
    thread = threadList->GetNext(thread);
    hThreads[uIndex] = thread->Handle();
  }

  WaitForMultipleObjects(threadList->Count(), hThreads, TRUE,
INFINITE);
  delete[] hThreads;
}

void CThreadPool::RemoveAll()
{
  CThread* thread = 0;
  while (thread = threadList->GetNext(thread))
  {
    threadList->Remove(thread);
    thread = 0;
  }
  delete threadList;
}

void CThreadPool::ReleaseThread(DWORD dwThreadId)
{
  CThread* thread = threadList->Find(CThread::GetThreadId,
dwThreadId);
  if (thread != NULL)
  {
    TerminateThread(thread->Handle(), (DWORD)-1);

  }
}

CThread* CThreadPool::RequestThread(LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE
lpThreadStart)
{
  CThread* thread = NULL;
  if (Count() < MaxCount())
  {
    threadList->Insert(thread = new CThread(lpThreadStart));
    return thread;
  }

  while (thread = threadList->GetNext(thread))
  {
    if (!thread->StillAlive())
    {
      break;
    }
    Sleep(100);
  }

  if (thread == NULL)
  {
    thread = threadList->GetFirst();
  }

  threadList->Remove(thread);

  threadList->Insert(thread = new CThread(lpThreadStart));
  return thread;
}

#endif

#include "main.h"
#include "CBankAccount.h"

#include "CThreadPool.h"

double Random(double dMin, double dMax)
{
  double dValue = (double)rand() / RAND_MAX;
  return dMin + dValue * (dMax - dMin);
}

int main(void)
{
  srand((unsigned)time(NULL));

#define ACCOUNTS_COUNT 12
  CBankAccount* accounts[ACCOUNTS_COUNT];
  for (unsigned uIndex = 0; uIndex < ACCOUNTS_COUNT; uIndex++)
  {
    accounts[uIndex] = new CBankAccount(Random(10, 1000));
  }

  CThreadPool* pool = new CThreadPool();

#define TASK_COUNT 5
  for (unsigned uIndex = 0; uIndex < TASK_COUNT; uIndex++)
  {
    int nFirstIndex = rand() % ACCOUNTS_COUNT;
    int nSecondIndex = -1;
    while ((nSecondIndex = rand() % ACCOUNTS_COUNT) ==
nFirstIndex){}

    CParameters* params = new CParameters(accounts[nFirstIndex],
accounts[nSecondIndex], Random(50, 200));
    pool->RequestThread(CBankAccount::Transfer)->Start(params);
  }

  pool->WaitAll();
  delete pool;

#ifdef _DEBUG
  return system("pause");
#endif
  return 0;
}

  if (parameters->dAmount < parameters->fromAccount->dBalance)
  {

  DWORD ContextThreadId() const {
    return pThreadContext->dwThreadId; }
  DWORD ExitStatus(){ GetExitCodeThread(hThread, &dwExitCode);
return dwExitCode; }
  CThread* SetMaxWaitTime(DWORD dwMilliseconds){
    pThreadContext->dwMaxWaitTime = dwMilliseconds;
  return this; }
  static DWORD GetThreadId(CThread* cThread);
protected:
  static DWORD WINAPI StartAddress(LPVOID lpParam);
private:
  typedef struct
  {
    LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE lpThreadStart;
    LPVOID lpParameter;
    HANDLE hThread;
    DWORD dwThreadId;
    DWORD dwDispatcherId;
    DWORD dwMaxWaitTime;
  } STARTCONTEXT, *PSTARTCONTEXT;
  HANDLE hThread;
  DWORD dwThreadId;
  DWORD dwExitCode;
  PSTARTCONTEXT pThreadContext;

};

CThread::CThread(LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE lpThreadStart, DWORD
dwDispatcherId) : dwExitCode(0)
{
  pThreadContext = new STARTCONTEXT();
  pThreadContext->lpThreadStart = lpThreadStart;
  pThreadContext->dwDispatcherId = dwDispatcherId;
  pThreadContext->dwMaxWaitTime = MAX_WAIT_TIME;
  hThread = CreateThread(NULL, 0, StartAddress, this,
    CREATE_SUSPENDED, &dwThreadId);
}

CThread::~CThread()
{
  delete pThreadContext;

  if (StillAlive())
  {
    TerminateThread(hThread, (DWORD)-1);
  }
  CloseHandle(hThread);
}

DWORD CThread::GetThreadId(CThread* cThread)
{
  return cThread->ThreadId();
}

DWORD WINAPI CThread::StartAddress(LPVOID lpParam)
{
  CThread* thread = (CThread*)lpParam;
  thread->pThreadContext->hThread = CreateThread(NULL, 0,
    thread->pThreadContext->lpThreadStart,
    thread->pThreadContext->lpParameter, 0,
    &thread->pThreadContext->dwThreadId);

  DWORD dwStatus = WaitForSingleObject(
    thread->pThreadContext->hThread,
    thread->pThreadContext->dwMaxWaitTime);

  CloseHandle(thread->pThreadContext->hThread);

  PostThreadMessage(thread->pThreadContext->dwDispatcherId,
    MSG_ENDTASK, (WPARAM)thread->dwThreadId, 0);
  return 0L;
}

#endif

#ifndef __THREADPOOL__

class CThreadPool
{
public:
  CThreadPool();
  CThreadPool(unsigned uMaxThreads);
  ~CThreadPool();
  DWORD Count(){ return threadList->Count(); }
  void RemoveThread(DWORD dwThreadId);
  void WaitAll();
  void RemoveAll();
  DWORD& MaxCount(){ return dwMaxCount; }
  void ReleaseThread(DWORD dwThreadId);
  CThread* RequestThread(LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE threadStart);
private:
  void InitializePool();
  static DWORD WINAPI ProblemSolver(LPVOID lpParam);
  void ClearMessageQueue(){ MSG msg; while (PeekMessage(&msg,
NULL, 0, 0, PM_REMOVE)); }
  HANDLE hProblemSolver;
  HANDLE hEvent;
  CList<CThread>* threadList;
  DWORD dwMaxCount;
};

CThreadPool::CThreadPool()
{
  SYSTEM_INFO sysInfo;
  GetSystemInfo(&sysInfo);
  dwMaxCount = sysInfo.dwNumberOfProcessors;

  InitializePool();

}

CThreadPool::CThreadPool(unsigned uMaxThreads)
{
  dwMaxCount = uMaxThreads;

  InitializePool();
}

CThreadPool::~CThreadPool()
{
  SetEvent(hEvent);

  if (WaitForSingleObject(hProblemSolver, MAX_WAIT_TIME) !=
    WAIT_OBJECT_0)
  {
    TerminateThread(hProblemSolver, (DWORD)-1);
  }
  CloseHandle(hProblemSolver);

  CloseHandle(hEvent);

  RemoveAll();
  ClearMessageQueue();
}
152CThreadPool.h — RemoveThread, WaitAll, RemoveAll, RequestThreadbook pp. 362–364 · PDF pp. 377–379▼
Verbatim listing from the PDF
void CThreadPool::RemoveThread(DWORD dwThreadId)
{
  CThread* thread = threadList->Find(CThread::GetThreadId,
dwThreadId);
  if (thread)
  {
    delete thread;
  }
}

void CThreadPool::WaitAll()
{
  HANDLE* hThreads = new HANDLE[threadList->Count()];
  CThread* thread = 0;

  for (unsigned uIndex = 0; uIndex < threadList->Count();
uIndex++)
  {

    thread = threadList->GetNext(thread);
    hThreads[uIndex] = thread->Handle();
  }

  WaitForMultipleObjects(threadList->Count(), hThreads, TRUE,
INFINITE);
  delete[] hThreads;
}

void CThreadPool::RemoveAll()
{
  CThread* thread = 0;
  while (thread = threadList->GetNext(thread))
  {
    threadList->Remove(thread);
    thread = 0;
  }
  delete threadList;
}

void CThreadPool::ReleaseThread(DWORD dwThreadId)
{
  CThread* thread = threadList->Find(CThread::GetThreadId,
dwThreadId);
  if (thread != NULL)
  {
    TerminateThread(thread->Handle(), (DWORD)-1);
  }
}

CThread* CThreadPool::RequestThread(LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE
threadStart)
{
  CThread* thread = NULL;
  if (Count() < MaxCount())
  {
    threadList->Insert(thread = new CThread(threadStart,
GetCurrentThreadId()));
    return thread;
  }

  while (thread = threadList->GetNext(thread))
  {
    if (!thread->StillAlive())
    {

      break;
    }
  }

  if (thread == NULL)
  {
    MSG msg = { 0 };
    while (GetMessage(&msg, NULL, 0, 0) > 0)
    {
      thread = threadList->Find(CThread::GetThreadId,
        (DWORD)msg.wParam);

      if (thread)
      {
        break;
      }
    }
  }

  threadList->Remove(thread);

  threadList->Insert(thread = new CThread(threadStart,
GetCurrentThreadId()));
  return thread;
}
153CThreadPool.h — InitializePool and the ProblemSolver loopbook pp. 364–365 · PDF pp. 379–380▼
Verbatim listing from the PDF
void CThreadPool::InitializePool()
{
  MSG msg;
  PeekMessage(&msg, NULL, WM_USER, WM_USER, PM_NOREMOVE);

  hEvent = CreateEvent(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, _T("__prbslv_1342__"));
  hProblemSolver = CreateThread(NULL, 0, ProblemSolver, this, 0,
NULL);

  threadList = new CList<CThread>();
}

DWORD WINAPI CThreadPool::ProblemSolver(LPVOID lpParam)
{
  CThreadPool* pool = (CThreadPool*)lpParam;

  DWORD dwWaitStatus = 0;
  while (true)
  {
    dwWaitStatus = WaitForSingleObject(pool->hEvent, 10);
    if (dwWaitStatus == WAIT_OBJECT_0)
    {
      break;

    }

    CThread* thread = NULL;
    while (thread = pool->threadList->GetNext(thread))
    {
      if (thread->StillAlive())
      {
        HWCT hWct = NULL;
        DWORD dwNodeCount = WCT_MAX_NODE_COUNT;
        BOOL bDeadlock = FALSE;
        WAITCHAIN_NODE_INFO NodeInfoArray[WCT_MAX_NODE_COUNT];

        hWct = OpenThreadWaitChainSession(0, NULL);
        if (GetThreadWaitChain(hWct, NULL,
          WCTP_GETINFO_ALL_FLAGS, thread->ContextThreadId(),
          &dwNodeCount, NodeInfoArray, &bDeadlock))
        {
          if (bDeadlock)
          {
            if (TerminateThread(thread->ContextHandle(),
(DWORD)-1))
            {
_tprintf_s(
#ifdef _UNICODE
  _T("%ws\n%ws\t[%u]%ws\n\n"),
#else
  _T("%s\n%s\t[%u]%s\n\n"),
#endif
  _T("Error! Deadlock found!"), _T("Thread:"),
  thread->ContextThreadId(), _T("terminated!"));

            }
          }
        }
        CloseThreadWaitChainSession(hWct);
      }
    }

    Sleep(1000);
  }
  return 0L;
}

#endif

#include "main.h"
#include "CBankAccount.h"
#include "CThreadPool.h"

int main(void)
{
  int i = 0;
  while (i++ < 10)
  {
    CBankAccount* a = new CBankAccount(200);
    CBankAccount* b = new CBankAccount(200);

    CThreadPool* pool = new CThreadPool(4);

    CParameters* params1 = new CParameters(a, b, 100);
    pool->RequestThread(
      CBankAccount::Transfer)->SetMaxWaitTime(
      6000)->Start(params1);

    CParameters* params2 = new CParameters(b, a, 50);
    pool->RequestThread(CBankAccount::Transfer)->Start(params2);

    pool->WaitAll();
    delete pool;
  }

#ifdef _DEBUG
  return system("pause");
#endif
  return 0;
}

156RemoteLoadLibrary — injecting LoadLibraryA into another processbook pp. 372–373 · PDF pp. 387–388▼
Verbatim listing from the PDF
#include <windows.h>
#include <tchar.h>
#include "..\common.h"

int __stdcall RemoteLoadLibrary(HANDLE hProcess, char*
szLibraryName)
{
  LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE lpLoadLibrary = (LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE)
GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandleA("Kernel32.dll"), "LoadLibraryA");
  if (lpLoadLibrary == NULL)
  {
    return -1;
  }

  if (hProcess == NULL)
  {
    _tprintf_s(_T("Handle to Process 0x%x was NULL!\n"), (int)
hProcess);
    return -1;
  }

  size_t uMemSize = strlen(szLibraryName) + 1;
  void* lpRemoteMem = VirtualAllocEx(hProcess, NULL, uMemSize,
MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE);
  if (lpRemoteMem == NULL)
  {
_tprintf_s(
#ifdef _UNICODE
  _T("%ws\nError:\t%u\n"),
#else
  _T("%s\nError:\t%u\n"),
#endif
  _T("Could not allocate remote virtual memory!"),
  GetLastError());
    return -1;
  }

  BOOL bSuccess = WriteProcessMemory(hProcess, lpRemoteMem,
szLibraryName, uMemSize, NULL);
  if (bSuccess == STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION || bSuccess == FALSE)
  {
    _tprintf_s(
      _T("Could not write remote virtual memory!\nError:\t%u\n"),
      GetLastError());
    VirtualFreeEx(hProcess, lpRemoteMem, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
    return -1;
  }

  HANDLE hThread = CreateRemoteThread(hProcess, NULL, 0,
lpLoadLibrary, lpRemoteMem, 0, NULL);
  if (hThread == NULL)
  {
    _tprintf_s(
      _T("Could not create remote thread!\nError:\t%u\n"),
      GetLastError());
    VirtualFreeEx(hProcess, lpRemoteMem, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
    return -1;
  }

  WaitForSingleObject(hThread, INFINITE);

  VirtualFreeEx(hProcess, lpRemoteMem, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
  CloseHandle(hThread);

  return 0;
}

}

{

  HANDLE hMapping = CreateFileMapping((HANDLE)-1, NULL,
    PAGE_READWRITE, 0, sizeof(COMM_OBJECT), MAPPING_NAME);
  HANDLE hEvent = CreateEvent(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, EVENT_NAME);

  STARTUPINFO startInfo = { 0 };

  BOOL bSuccess = CreateProcess(
    _T("C:\\Windows\\System32\\calc.exe"), NULL, NULL,
    NULL, FALSE, 0, NULL, NULL, &startInfo, &processInfo);

  if (!bSuccess)
  {
    _tprintf_s(_T("Error:\t%u\n"), GetLastError());
  }
  else
  {
    WaitForSingleObject(processInfo.hThread, 500);
    RemoteLoadLibrary(processInfo.hProcess, szLibrary);

    WaitForSingleObject(hEvent, INFINITE);

    PCOMM_OBJECT pCommObject = (PCOMM_OBJECT)
MapViewOfFile(hMapping, FILE_MAP_READ, 0, 0, 0);

    if (pCommObject)
    {

      RemoteFreeLibrary(processInfo.hProcess,
        pCommObject->hLibrary);
    }
  }

  CloseHandle(hEvent);
  CloseHandle(hMapping);

#ifdef _DEBUG
  return system("pause");

  return 0;
}

#include <Windows.h>
#include <tchar.h>
#include "..\common.h"

typedef struct
{
  DWORD dwProcessId;
  HWND hWnd;
} WINDOW_INFORMATION, *PWINDOW_INFORMATION;

BOOL IsMainWindow(HWND hWnd)
{
  return GetWindow(hWnd, GW_OWNER) == (HWND)0 &&
IsWindowVisible(hWnd);
}

BOOL CALLBACK EnumWindowsCallback(HWND hWnd, LPARAM lParam)
{
  PWINDOW_INFORMATION pWindowInformation = (PWINDOW_INFORMATION)
lParam;
  DWORD dwProcessId = 0;

  GetWindowThreadProcessId(hWnd, &dwProcessId);

  if (pWindowInformation->dwProcessId == dwProcessId &&
IsMainWindow(hWnd))
  {
    pWindowInformation->hWnd = hWnd;
    return FALSE;
  }

  return TRUE;
}

HWND FindMainWindow()
{
  WINDOW_INFORMATION wndInfo = { GetCurrentProcessId(), 0 };

  EnumWindows(EnumWindowsCallback, (LPARAM)&wndInfo);

  return wndInfo.hWnd;
}

void ChangeWindowTitle()
{
  HWND hWnd = FindMainWindow();
  if (hWnd)
  {
    SetWindowText(hWnd,
      _T("Remotely started thread inside calculator!"));
  }
}

BOOL WINAPI DllMain(HINSTANCE hInstance, DWORD dwReason, LPVOID
lpReserved)
{
  switch (dwReason)
  {
    case DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH:
    {
      HANDLE hMapping = OpenFileMapping(FILE_MAP_ALL_ACCESS,
FALSE, MAPPING_NAME);
      if (hMapping)
      {
        PCOMM_OBJECT pCommObject = (PCOMM_OBJECT)
MapViewOfFile(hMapping, FILE_MAP_ALL_ACCESS, 0, 0, 0);
        if (pCommObject)

        {
          pCommObject->hLibrary = hInstance;
        }

        CloseHandle(hMapping);
      }

      ChangeWindowTitle();

      HANDLE hEvent = OpenEvent(EVENT_ALL_ACCESS, FALSE,
        EVENT_NAME);
      if (hEvent)
      {
        SetEvent(hEvent);
        CloseHandle(hEvent);
      }
      break;
    }

    case DLL_PROCESS_DETACH:
    {
      //
      break;
    }
  }
  return TRUE;
}

56 Appendix — Building the book's examples

The last part of the book is a setup guide, not another theory chapter. It walks through installing MySQL Connector/C, the Windows Driver Kit 8.1, configuring a kernel-driver project, watching driver output with DebugView, and enabling OpenMP in Visual Studio.

01 / DATABASE

MySQL Connector/C 6.1.3

Download the 32- or 64-bit MSI, add include and libmysql.lib, and copy libmysql.dll to System32.

02 / KIT

WDK 8.1 for VS 2013

Install the kit, then point the driver project at the kernel headers and libraries under Windows Kits\8.1.

03 / DRIVER

.sys instead of .exe

Change the target extension, preprocessor definitions, calling convention, subsystem, entry point and base address.

04 / OUTPUT

DebugView

Enable Capture Kernel (Ctrl+K) to see the output of DbgPrint from a kernel driver.

05 / OPENMP

Three switches

/MP, /Qpar and /openmp turn on multi-processor compilation, parallel code generation and OpenMP.

06 / SCOPE

All screenshots included

The appendix contains no C++ listings — only setup paths and URLs. Its 1 verbatim line card and 19 screenshots are embedded below.

58 Appendix: detailed setup summary

Installing MySQL Connector/C

  • Download mysql-connector-c-6.1.3-win32.msi or -winx64.msi from the MySQL Connector/C downloads page and run a Complete installation.
  • In the MultithreadedDBTest properties, add C:\Program Files\MySQL\MySQL Connector C 6.1\include under Additional Include Directories.
  • Under Linker → Input → Additional Dependencies add C:\Program Files\MySQL\MySQL Connector C 6.1\lib\libmysql.lib.
  • Copy libmysql.dll from that lib folder into C:\Windows\System32, then the database example from Chapter 2 will build and run.

Installing the Windows Driver Kit

  • The book targets Visual Studio 2013, so it uses WDK 8.1, downloaded from Microsoft's hardware developer page (or the short link go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=393659).
  • Run the installer, opt in or out of the Customer Experience Improvement Program, accept the licence, and wait for the wizard to finish.

Configuring the kernel-driver project

  • Open the KernelThread solution from Chapter 2. For the DriverApp project set Target Extension from .exe to .sys.
  • Set Additional Include Directories to C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\8.1\Include\km and replace Preprocessor Definitions with _X86_ or _AMD64_ to match the active configuration.
  • Clear Enable C++ Exceptions, set Basic Runtime Checks to Default, disable the security check (/GS-), and choose the __stdcall calling convention (/Gz).
  • Disable incremental linking, add ntoskrnl.lib and hal.lib from Windows Kits\8.1\Lib\win8\km\<arch>, disable manifest generation (/MANIFEST:NO), and set SubSystem to Native (/SUBSYSTEM:NATIVE) with Driver = Driver (/Driver).
  • Finally set Entry Point to DriverEntry, Base Address to 0x10000, clear Randomize Base Address and Data Execution Prevention, and set Import Library to ntoskrnl.lib.
  • On 64-bit Windows an unsigned driver will not load until Advanced Boot Options → Disable Driver Signature Enforcement (F8) is used; that choice lasts only for the current session.

Watching the driver with DebugView

  • Download the DebugView ZIP from Sysinternals and extract it. In the menu choose Capture → Capture Kernel or press Ctrl+K.
  • Run the KernelDriver project and the driver's debug output appears in DebugView.

Enabling OpenMP

  • Open the ConcurrentDesign solution from Chapter 7 and its project properties.
  • Under C/C++ → General set Multi-processor Compilation to Yes (/MP).
  • Under Code Generation set Enable Parallel Code Generation to Yes (/Qpar).
  • Under Language set Open MP Support to Yes (/openmp). The OpenMP version of Schwefel's function can then compile and run.
Book's final message: these are the practical foundations behind all eight chapters. Concurrency needs OS, compiler, OOP and C++ knowledge — and practice is the best teacher.
